container.Description: The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The container name.

network_driver.caption: Network Driver
network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.caption: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.caption: Pod UUID
pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.caption: Runtime
runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.caption: Image Tag
tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

cpu_info.Name: cpu_info
cpu_info.Caption: CPU Information
cpu_info.Description: The CPU information object contains attributes describing a physical CPU package installed in the device.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

1.caption: x86
1.description: CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

2.caption: ARM
2.description: CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

3.caption: RISC-V
3.description: CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The number of bits used by the CPU for memory addressing.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the CPU. For example: Intel Xeon Gold 6348, AMD EPYC 7763, or Apple M3 Max.

speed_mhz.caption: Compute Unit Speed (MHz)
speed_mhz.description: The nominal clock speed of the unit, expressed in megahertz.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the CPU. For example: Intel, AMD, or Apple.

cve.Name: cve
cve.Caption: CVE
cve.Description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in CVE Program catalog (CVE). There is one CVE Record for each vulnerability in the catalog.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.caption: CWE UID
cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.caption: CWE URL
cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration details related to the CVE Record.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.caption: Vulnerability Type
type.description:
The vulnerability type as classified in the CVE catalog.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.caption: CVE ID
uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

cvss.Name: cvss
cvss.Caption: CVSS Score
cvss.Description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) object provides a way to capture the principal characteristics of a vulnerability and produce a numerical score reflecting its severity.

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.caption: CVSS Depth
depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.caption: Overall Score
overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL for the CVSS score. For example: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228

vector_string.caption: Vector String
vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor that provided the CVSS score. For example: NVD, REDHAT etc.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CVSS version. For example: 3.1.

cwe.Name: cwe
cwe.Caption: CWE
cwe.Description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

caption.caption: Caption
caption.description: The caption assigned to the Common Weakness Enumeration unique identifier.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: URL pointing to the CWE Specification. For more information see CWE.

uid.caption: CWE ID
uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration unique number assigned to a specific weakness. A CWE Identifier begins "CWE" followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CWE-123.

d3f_tactic.Name: d3f_tactic
d3f_tactic.Caption: Defensive Tactic
d3f_tactic.Description: The Defensive Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The tactic name that is associated with the defensive technique. For example: Isolate.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive tactic. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/tactic/d3f:Isolate/

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive tactic.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

d3f_technique.Name: d3f_technique
d3f_technique.Caption: Defensive Technique
d3f_technique.Description: The Defensive Technique object describes the leaf defensive technique ID and/or name associated to a countermeasure.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the defensive technique. For example: IO Port Restriction.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive technique. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:IOPortRestriction/

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive technique. For example: D3-IOPR.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

d3fend.Name: d3fend
d3fend.Caption: Defensive Countermeasure
d3fend.Description: The Defensive Countermeasure object describes the tactic & technique associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_tactic.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Tactic
d3f_tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_technique.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Technique
d3f_technique.description: The Technique object describes the technique ID and/or name associated with a countermeasure.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The D3FEND™ Matrix version.

data_classification.Name: data_classification
data_classification.Caption: Data Classification
data_classification.Description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The type is not mapped. See the data_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Personal
1.description: Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Electronic Personal Health Information (ePHI), or similarly personal information. E.g., full name, home address, date of birth, etc.

2.caption: Governmental
2.description: Any sensitive government identification number related to a person or other classified material. E.g., Passport numbers, driver license numbers, business identification, taxation identifiers, etc.

3.caption: Financial
3.description: Any financially-related sensitive information or Cardholder Data (CHD). E.g., banking account numbers, credit card numbers, International Banking Account Numbers (IBAN), SWIFT codes, etc.

4.caption: Business
4.description: Any business-specific sensitive data such as intellectual property, trademarks, copyrights, human resource data, Board of Directors meeting minutes, and similar.

5.caption: Military and Law Enforcement
5.description: Any mission-specific sensitive data for military, law enforcement, or other government agencies such as specifically classified data, weapon systems information, or other planning data.

6.caption: Security
6.description: Any sensitive security-related data such as passwords, passkeys, IP addresses, API keys, credentials and similar secrets. E.g., AWS Access Secret Key, SaaS API Keys, user passwords, database credentials, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: Any other type of data classification or a multi-variate classification made up of several other classification categories.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

discovery_details.caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the data policy that governs data handling and security measures related to classification.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.caption: Status Details
status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

1.caption: Complete
1.description: The classification job completed for the evaluated resource.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: The classification job partially completed for the evaluated resource.

3.caption: Fail
3.description: The classification job failed for the evaluated resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification job type id is not mapped.

total.caption: Total
total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

data_security.Name: data_security
data_security.Caption: Data Security
data_security.Description: The Data Security object describes the characteristics, techniques and content of a Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Data Loss Detection (DLD), Data Classification, or similar tools' finding, alert, or detection mechanism(s).

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The type is not mapped. See the data_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Personal
1.description: Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Electronic Personal Health Information (ePHI), or similarly personal information. E.g., full name, home address, date of birth, etc.

2.caption: Governmental
2.description: Any sensitive government identification number related to a person or other classified material. E.g., Passport numbers, driver license numbers, business identification, taxation identifiers, etc.

3.caption: Financial
3.description: Any financially-related sensitive information or Cardholder Data (CHD). E.g., banking account numbers, credit card numbers, International Banking Account Numbers (IBAN), SWIFT codes, etc.

4.caption: Business
4.description: Any business-specific sensitive data such as intellectual property, trademarks, copyrights, human resource data, Board of Directors meeting minutes, and similar.

5.caption: Military and Law Enforcement
5.description: Any mission-specific sensitive data for military, law enforcement, or other government agencies such as specifically classified data, weapon systems information, or other planning data.

6.caption: Security
6.description: Any sensitive security-related data such as passwords, passkeys, IP addresses, API keys, credentials and similar secrets. E.g., AWS Access Secret Key, SaaS API Keys, user passwords, database credentials, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: Any other type of data classification or a multi-variate classification made up of several other classification categories.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

data_lifecycle_state.caption: Data Lifecycle State
data_lifecycle_state.description: The name of the stage or state that the data was in. E.g., Data-at-Rest, Data-in-Transit, etc.

data_lifecycle_state_id.caption: Data Lifecycle State ID
data_lifecycle_state_id.description: The stage or state that the data was in when it was assessed or scanned by a data security tool.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The data lifecycle state is unknown.

1.caption: Data at-Rest
1.description: The data was stored on physical or logical media and was not actively moving through the network nor was being processed. E.g., data stored in a database, PDF files in a file share, or EHR records in object storage.

2.caption: Data in-Transit
2.description: The data was actively moving through the network or from one physical or logical location to another. E.g., emails being send, data replication or Change Data Capture (CDC) streams, or sensitive data processed on an API.

3.caption: Data in-Use
3.description: The data was being processed, accessed, or read by a system, making it active in memory or CPU. E.g., sensitive data in a Business Intelligence tool, ePHI being processed in an EHR application or a user viewing data stored in a spreadsheet or PDF.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The data lifecycle state is not mapped. See the data_lifecycle_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: Specific pattern, algorithm, fingerprint, or model used for detection.

detection_system.caption: Detection System
detection_system.description: The data security tool or system that the finding, detection, or alert originated from, normalized to the caption of detection_system_id. E.g., Endpoint, Secure Email Gateway, etc.

detection_system_id.caption: Detection System ID
detection_system_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data security tool or system type from which the finding, detection, or alert originated. When the type is not listed, use 99 (Other) and populate detection_system with the source-specific label.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The detection system type is Unknown.

1.caption: Endpoint
1.description: A dedicated agent or sensor installed on a device, either a dedicated data security tool or an Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies. E.g., Forcepoint DLP, Symantec DLP, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE).

10.caption: Application-Level DLP
10.description: A built in Data Loss Prevention (DLP) or other data security capability within a tool or platform such as an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) or Customer Relations Management (CRM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies.

11.caption: Developer Security
11.description: Any Developer Security tool such as an Infrastructure-as-Code (IAC) security scanner, Secrets Detection, or Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies. E.g., TruffleHog, GitGuardian, Git-Secrets.

12.caption: Data Security Posture Management
12.description: A Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) tool is a continuous monitoring and data discovery solution that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies for local and cloud environments. E.g., Cyera, Sentra, IBM Polar Security.

2.caption: DLP Gateway
2.description: A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) gateway that is positioned in-line of an information store such as a network share, a database, or otherwise that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies.

3.caption: Mobile Device Management
3.description: A Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies on mobile devices (e.g., cellphones, tablets, End User Devices [EUDs]).

4.caption: Data Discovery & Classification
4.description: A tool that actively identifies and classifies sensitive data in digital media and information stores in accordance with a policy or automated functionality. E.g, Amazon Macie, Microsoft Purview.

5.caption: Secure Web Gateway
5.description: A Secure Web Gateway (SWG) is any tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies at a network-edge such as within a proxy or firewall service.

6.caption: Secure Email Gateway
6.description: A Secure Email Gateway (SEG) is any tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies within email systems. E.g., Microsoft Defender for Office, Google Workspaces.

7.caption: Digital Rights Management
7.description: A Digital Rights Management (DRM) or a dedicated Information Rights Management (IRM) are tools which can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies on digital media via policy or user access rights.

8.caption: Cloud Access Security Broker
8.description: A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies in-line to cloud systems such as the public cloud or Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) tool. E.g., Forcepoint CASB, SkyHigh Security.

9.caption: Database Activity Monitoring
9.description: A Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) tool that can detect sensitive data and/or enforce data security policies as part of a dedicated database or warehouse monitoring solution.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The detection system type is not mapped. See the detection_system attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

discovery_details.caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

pattern_match.caption: Pattern Match
pattern_match.description: A text, binary, file name, or datastore that matched against a detection rule.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the policy that triggered the finding.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.caption: Status Details
status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

1.caption: Complete
1.description: The classification job completed for the evaluated resource.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: The classification job partially completed for the evaluated resource.

3.caption: Fail
3.description: The classification job failed for the evaluated resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification job type id is not mapped.

total.caption: Total
total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

database.Name: database
database.Caption: Database
database.Description: The database object is used for databases which are typically datastore services that contain an organized collection of structured and unstructured data or a types of data.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the database was known to have been created.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the database.

embedding_model.caption: Embedding Model
embedding_model.description: Model used for creating embeddings (if applicable). For example: text-embedding-ada-002 or all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The group names to which the database belongs.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the database.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The database name, ordinarily as assigned by a database administrator.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the database in bytes.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The database type.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the database type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the database.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

databucket.Name: databucket
databucket.Caption: Databucket
databucket.Description: The databucket object is a basic container that holds data, typically organized through the use of data partitions.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description: The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the databucket is located.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the databucket was known to have been created.

criticality.caption: Criticality
criticality.description: The criticality of the databucket as defined by the event source.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the databucket.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the databucket. Should be populated if the databucket is encrypted.

file.caption: File
file.description: Details about the file/object within a databucket.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related resource group.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The group names to which the databucket belongs.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified hostname of the databucket.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the resource, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

is_encrypted.caption: Encrypted
is_encrypted.description: Indicates if the databucket is encrypted.

is_public.caption: Public
is_public.description: Indicates if the databucket is publicly accessible.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when any changes, updates, or modifications were made within the databucket.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The databucket name.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the databucket.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The cloud region of the databucket.

resource_relationship.caption: Resource Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this databucket relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the databucket in bytes.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The databucket type.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the databucket type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the databucket.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the resource. For example 1.2.3.

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description: The specific availability zone within a cloud region where the databucket is located.

dce_rpc.Name: dce_rpc
dce_rpc.Caption: DCE/RPC
dce_rpc.Description: The DCE/RPC, or Distributed Computing Environment/Remote Procedure Call, object describes the remote procedure call system for distributed computing environments.

command_response.caption: Command Response
command_response.description: The reply to the request command (e.g. RESPONSE, BINDACK or FAULT).

opnum.caption: Opnum
opnum.description: An operation number used to identify a specific remote procedure call (RPC) method or a method in an interface.

rpc_interface.caption: Remote Procedure Call Interface
rpc_interface.description: The RPC Interface object describes the details pertaining to the remote procedure call interface.

delegation.Name: delegation
delegation.Caption: Delegation
delegation.Description: A durable authorization context that a principal issues to a delegate (e.g., an application, automated process, service account, or AI agent), representing delegated authority to act on the principal's behalf. Persists independently of any single trace, session, or workflow instance, so the same delegation can be referenced across many events. The principal and delegate themselves are identified by the other objects on the event carrying this delegation, such as actor.user or actor.iam_role for the principal and ai_operation.ai_agent for an AI delegate. The delegation object itself only carries the durable identifiers used to correlate across those events. Delegations reference a parent via parent_uid, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of re-delegations that supports lineage queries across the chain of authority. This authority graph is distinct from any agent instantiation or orchestration hierarchy, which may or may not coincide with it.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the delegation was issued by the issuing authority.

issuer_uid.caption: Issuer ID
issuer_uid.description: The unique identifier of the trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, orchestration gateway, or SDK wrapper) that generated this delegation. Enables verification that delegation IDs were issued by an authorized component rather than self-asserted by the delegate.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Delegation ID
parent_uid.description: The delegation identifier of the parent delegation, if this delegation was created by re-delegating authority to another party (e.g., a downstream service or automated process). This creates a parent-child relationship that enables tracking the complete chain of delegation ancestry. Does not indicate that the delegate was instantiated or spawned by the parent's delegate; that relationship, if any, is tracked separately.

uid.caption: Delegation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier for this delegation context. Must be stable across the lifetime of the delegation and generated by a trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, or orchestration gateway) rather than self-asserted by the delegate. All events executed under this delegation share this identifier.

device.Name: device
device.Caption: Device
device.Description: The Device object represents an addressable computer system or host, which is typically connected to a computer network and participates in the transmission or processing of data within the computer network.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autoscale_uid.caption: Autoscale UID
autoscale_uid.description: The unique identifier of the cloud autoscale configuration.

boot_time.caption: Boot Time
boot_time.description: The time the system was booted.

boot_uid.caption: Boot UID
boot_uid.description: A unique identifier of the device that changes after every reboot. For example, the value of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id from Linux's procfs.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the device, ordinarily as reported by the operating system.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The network domain where the device resides. For example: work.example.com.

eid.caption: EID
eid.description: An Embedded Identity Document, is a unique serial number that identifies an eSIM-enabled device.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The group names to which the device belongs. For example: ["Windows Laptops", "Engineering"].

hypervisor.caption: Hypervisor
hypervisor.description: The name of the hypervisor running on the device. For example, Xen, VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox, etc.

iccid.caption: ICCID
iccid.description: The Integrated Circuit Card Identification of a mobile device. Typically it is a unique 18 to 22 digit number that identifies a SIM card.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The image used as a template to run the virtual machine.

imei.caption: IMEI
imei.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity that is associated with the device.

imei_list.caption: IMEI List
imei_list.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity values that are associated with the device.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The device IP address, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

is_compliant.caption: Compliant Device
is_compliant.description: The event occurred on a compliant device.

is_managed.caption: Managed Device
is_managed.description: The event occurred on a managed device.

is_mobile_account_active.caption: Mobile Account Active
is_mobile_account_active.description: Indicates whether the device has an active mobile account. For example, this is indicated by the itunesStoreAccountActive value within JAMF Pro mobile devices.

is_personal.caption: Personal Device
is_personal.description: The event occurred on a personal device.

is_shared.caption: Shared Device
is_shared.description: The event occurred on a shared device.

is_supervised.caption: Supervised Device
is_supervised.description: The event occurred on a supervised device. Devices that are supervised are typically mobile devices managed by a Mobile Device Management solution and are restricted from specific behaviors such as Apple AirDrop.

is_trusted.caption: Trusted Device
is_trusted.description: The event occurred on a trusted device.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the device.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

meid.caption: MEID
meid.description: The Mobile Equipment Identifier. It's a unique number that identifies a Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) mobile device.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model of the device. For example ThinkPad X1 Carbon.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the device was last known to have been modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description:
The alternate device name, ordinarily as assigned by an administrator.

Note: The Name could be any other string that helps to identify the device, such as a phone number; for example 310-555-1234.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

network_interfaces.caption: Network Interfaces
network_interfaces.description:
The physical or virtual network interfaces that are associated with the device, one for each unique MAC address/IP address/hostname/name combination.

Note: The first element of the array is the network information that pertains to the event.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the device.

os_machine_uuid.caption: OS Machine UUID
os_machine_uuid.description: The operating system assigned Machine ID. In Windows, this is the value stored at the registry path: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid. In Linux, this is stored in the file: /etc/machine-id.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

peripheral_devices.caption: Peripheral Device
peripheral_devices.description: The peripheral devices that are attached or connected to the device.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The region where the virtual machine is located. For example, an AWS Region.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The device type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The device type ID.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

udid.caption: Unique Device Identifier
udid.description: The Apple assigned Unique Device Identifier (UDID). For iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS devices, this is the UDID. For macOS devices, it is the Provisioning UDID. For example: 00008020-008D4548007B4F26

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the device. For example the Windows TargetSID or AWS EC2 ARN.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: An alternate unique identifier of the device if any. For example the ActiveDirectory DN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor for the device. For example Dell or Lenovo.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

device_hw_info.Name: device_hw_info
device_hw_info.Caption: Device Hardware Info
device_hw_info.Description: The Device Hardware Information object contains details and specifications of the physical components that make up a device. This information provides an overview of the hardware capabilities, configuration, and characteristics of the device.

bios_ver.caption: BIOS Version
bios_ver.description: The BIOS version. For example: LENOVO G5ETA2WW (2.62).

chassis.caption: Chassis
chassis.description: The chassis type describes the system enclosure or physical form factor. For example, as described for a Windows chassis type.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The total number of processor cores across all installed CPUs on the system. For per-CPU core detail, use cpu_info_list.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

1.caption: x86
1.description: CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

2.caption: ARM
2.description: CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

3.caption: RISC-V
3.description: CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

cpu_cores.caption: CPU Cores
cpu_cores.description: The number of processor cores in all installed processors. For Example: 42.

cpu_count.caption: CPU Count
cpu_count.description: The number of physical processors on a system. For per-CPU detail, use cpu_info_list.

cpu_info_list.caption: CPU Information
cpu_info_list.description: A list of cpu_info objects, each describing a physical CPU package installed in the device. Use with cpu_count.

cpu_speed.caption: Processor Speed
cpu_speed.description: The speed of the processor in Mhz. For Example: 4200.

cpu_type.caption: Processor Type
cpu_type.description: The processor type. For example: x86 Family 6 Model 37 Stepping 5.

desktop_display.caption: Desktop Display
desktop_display.description: The desktop display affiliated with the event

gpu_count.caption: GPU Count
gpu_count.description: The number of graphics processors on a system. For per-GPU detail, use gpu_info_list.

gpu_info_list.caption: GPU information
gpu_info_list.description: A list of GPU objects describing the hardware properties of each graphics processor installed on the device. Use with gpu_count.

ram_size.caption: RAM Size
ram_size.description: The total amount of installed RAM, in Megabytes. For example: 2048.

uuid.caption: UUID
uuid.description: The device manufacturer assigned universally unique hardware identifier. For SMBIOS compatible devices such as those running Linux and Windows, it is the UUID member of the System Information structure in the SMBIOS information. For macOS devices, it is the Hardware UUID (also known as IOPlatformUUID in the I/O Registry).

digital_signature.Name: digital_signature
digital_signature.Caption: Digital Signature
digital_signature.Description: The Digital Signature object contains information about the cryptographic mechanism used to verify the authenticity, integrity, and origin of the file or application.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The digital signature algorithm used to create the signature, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized digital signature algorithm.

1.caption: DSA
1.description: Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA).

2.caption: RSA
2.description: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) Algorithm.

3.caption: ECDSA
3.description: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm.

4.caption: Authenticode
4.description: Authenticode Digital Signature Algorithm.

5.caption: Code Signing
5.description: Code Signing Algorithm.

6.caption: App Package
6.description: Application Package Signing Algorithm.

certificate.caption: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate object containing information about the digital certificate.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the digital signature was created.

developer_uid.caption: Developer UID
developer_uid.description: The developer ID on the certificate that signed the file.

digest.caption: Message Digest
digest.description: The message digest attribute contains the fixed length message hash representation and the corresponding hashing algorithm information.

serialization.caption: Serialization
serialization.description: The canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

serialization_id.caption: Serialization ID
serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the signing input. Use Flat where the signed data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were signed; some signing formats (e.g. Authenticode) define their own canonicalization and populate both fields.

1.caption: Flat
1.description: No canonical serialization or signing envelope was applied; the signature is computed over the data's raw byte sequence, such as the content of a disk file or any other opaque byte stream.

2.caption: JCS
2.description: JSON Canonicalization Scheme - deterministic JSON serialization of the structured data prior to signing.

3.caption: JWS
3.description: JSON Web Signature - the JWS Signing Input, i.e. BASE64URL(protected header) '.' BASE64URL(payload).

4.caption: COSE
4.description: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption - the CBOR Sig_structure used as the binary signing input.

5.caption: DSSE
5.description: Dead Simple Signing Envelope - the PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) canonical signing input. Note: DSSE is a signing-envelope scheme, not a hash algorithm; any payload hash is carried separately in the fingerprint object.

6.caption: Authenticode
6.description: The Portable Executable (PE) Image Hash procedure that canonicalizes the PE structure into the byte sequence fed to the digest, excluding specified header fields and digesting sections in a defined order. Authenticode bundles canonicalization and signing format: when used, algorithm_id is also set to the Authenticode enum value.

7.caption: Code Signing
7.description: The procedure that describes how hashes of code and other structures form the Code Directory message that is signed. When used, algorithm_id is also set to the Code Signing enum value.

8.caption: App Package
8.description: The Windows Application Package signing procedure that describes how file hashes are stored in the manifest, and how that manifest is signed.

signature_value.caption: Signature Value
signature_value.description: The digital signature bytes, Base64-encoded. For enveloped schemes identified by serialization_id (JWS, COSE, DSSE), this carries the complete detached envelope; for Flat or JCS schemes it carries the raw signature over the signed byte sequence.

state.caption: State
state.description: The digital signature state defines the signature state, normalized to the caption of 'state_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized identifier of the signature state.

1.caption: Valid
1.description: The digital signature is valid.

10.caption: Broken
10.description: The digital signature is malformed and could not be processed.

2.caption: Expired
2.description: The digital signature is invalid because its timestamp does not fall within the certificate's validity period.

3.caption: Revoked
3.description: The digital signature is invalid due to certificate revocation.

4.caption: Suspended
4.description: The digital signature is invalid due to certificate suspension.

5.caption: Pending
5.description: The digital signature state is pending.

6.caption: Untrusted
6.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is rooted in an untrusted CA or is an untrusted self-signed certificate.

7.caption: Distrusted
7.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is explicitly distrusted. Note that whereas revocation is global, distrust reflects local IT/security policy.

8.caption: WrongUsage
8.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is not intended for code signing purposes.

9.caption: Bad
9.description: The digital signature is cryptographically invalid, e.g. a mismatched digest. This indicates possible tampering.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

discovery_details.Name: discovery_details
discovery_details.Caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.Description: The Discovery Details object describes results of a discovery task/job. Each result may be due to the violation of a rule associated with a policy and have multiple occurrences.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of discovered entities of the specified type.

occurrence_details.caption: Occurrence Details
occurrence_details.description: Details about where in the target entity, specified information was discovered. Only the attributes, relevant to the target entity type should be populated.

occurrences.caption: Occurrences
occurrences.description: Details about where in the target entity, specified information was discovered. Only the attributes, relevant to the target entity type should be populated.

rule.caption: Rule
rule.description: The rule associated with this discovery, usually part of the higher level policy from an enclosing class or object.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The specific type of information that was discovered. e.g. name, phone_number, etc.

value.caption: Value
value.description: Optionally, the specific value of discovered information.

display.Name: display
display.Caption: Display
display.Description: The Display object contains information about the physical or virtual display connected to a computer system.

physical_height.caption: Physical Height
physical_height.description: The numeric physical height of display.

physical_orientation.caption: Physical Orientation
physical_orientation.description: The numeric physical orientation of display.

physical_width.caption: Physical Width
physical_width.description: The numeric physical width of display.

scale_factor.caption: Scale Factor
scale_factor.description: The numeric scale factor of display.

dns_answer.Name: dns_answer
dns_answer.Caption: DNS Answer
dns_answer.Description: The DNS Answer object represents a specific response provided by the Domain Name System (DNS) when querying for information about a domain or performing a DNS operation. It encapsulates the relevant details and data returned by the DNS server in response to a query.

class.caption: Resource Record Class
class.description: The class of DNS data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

flag_ids.caption: DNS Header Flags
flag_ids.description: The list of DNS answer header flag IDs.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The flag is not mapped. See the flags attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

flags.caption: DNS Header Flags
flags.description: The list of DNS answer header flags.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The owner name of the resource record. For example: www.example.com.

packet_uid.caption: Packet UID
packet_uid.description: The DNS packet identifier assigned by the program that generated the query. The identifier is copied to the response.

rdata.caption: DNS RData
rdata.description: The data describing the DNS resource. The meaning of this data depends on the type and class of the resource record.

ttl.caption: TTL
ttl.description: The time interval that the resource record may be cached. Zero value means that the resource record can only be used for the transaction in progress, and should not be cached.

type.caption: Resource Record Type
type.description: The type of data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: CNAME.

dns_query.Name: dns_query
dns_query.Caption: DNS Query
dns_query.Description: The DNS Query object represents a specific request made to the Domain Name System (DNS) to retrieve information about a domain or perform a DNS operation.

class.caption: Resource Record Class
class.description: The class of resource records being queried. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname or domain being queried. For example: www.example.com

opcode.caption: DNS Opcode
opcode.description: The DNS opcode specifies the type of the query message.

opcode_id.caption: DNS Opcode ID
opcode_id.description: The DNS opcode ID specifies the normalized query message type as defined in RFC 5395.

1.caption: Inverse Query
1.description: Inverse query, obsolete

2.caption: Status
2.description: Server status request

3.caption: Reserved
3.description: Reserved, not used

4.caption: Notify
4.description: Zone change notification

5.caption: Update
5.description: Dynamic DNS update

6.caption: DSO Message
6.description: DNS Stateful Operations (DSO)

99.caption: Other
99.description: The DNS Opcode is not defined by the RFC. See the opcode attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

packet_uid.caption: Packet UID
packet_uid.description: The DNS packet identifier assigned by the program that generated the query. The identifier is copied to the response.

type.caption: Resource Record Type
type.description: The type of resource records being queried. See RFC 1035. For example: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, and NS.

dns_resource_record.Name: dns_resource_record
dns_resource_record.Caption: DNS Resource Record
dns_resource_record.Description: The DNS Resource Record object represents a single resource record as defined in RFC 1035. It is used in the Answer, Authority, and Additional sections of a DNS message.

class.caption: Resource Record Class
class.description: The class of DNS data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: IN.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The owner name of the resource record. For example: www.example.com.

rdata.caption: DNS RData
rdata.description: The data describing the DNS resource. The meaning of this data depends on the type and class of the resource record.

ttl.caption: TTL
ttl.description: The time interval that the resource record may be cached. Zero value means that the resource record can only be used for the transaction in progress, and should not be cached.

type.caption: Resource Record Type
type.description: The type of data contained in this resource record. See RFC 1035. For example: CNAME.

dns_section.Name: dns_section
dns_section.Caption: DNS Section
dns_section.Description: The DNS Section object represents a DNS message section that carries supplementary resource records alongside an optional TSIG record. It is used for both the client Additional section (query_additional) and the server Additional section (response_additional) of a DNS message. A DNS message has at most one TSIG record, which authenticates the entire message.

records.caption: Resource Records
records.description: The resource records contained in this DNS section.

tsig.caption: TSIG
tsig.description: The TSIG (Transaction Signature) record present in this DNS section, used to authenticate the entire DNS message. Per RFC 2845, at most one TSIG record is permitted per DNS message.

domain_contact.Name: domain_contact
domain_contact.Caption: Domain Contact
domain_contact.Description: The contact information related to a domain registration, e.g., registrant, administrator, abuse, billing, or technical contact.

location.caption: Contact Location Information
location.description: Location details for the contract such as the city, state/province, country, etc.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The individual or organization name for the contact.

phone_number.caption: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The number associated with the phone.

type.caption: Domain Contact Type
type.description: The Domain Contact type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source

type_id.caption: Domain Contact Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized domain contact type ID.

1.caption: Registrant
1.description: The contact information provided is for the domain registrant.

2.caption: Administrative
2.description: The contact information provided is for the domain administrator.

3.caption: Technical
3.description: The contact information provided is for the domain technical lead.

4.caption: Billing
4.description: The contact information provided is for the domain billing lead.

5.caption: Abuse
5.description: The contact information provided is for the domain abuse contact.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the contact information, typically provided in WHOIS information.

download_info.Name: download_info
download_info.Caption: Download Info
download_info.Description: The Download Info object contains metadata pertaining to a downloaded file.

referrer.caption: HTTP Referrer
referrer.description: The URL that referred to src_url. This is typically the URL of a web page containing a download link.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Information about the network endpoint from which the file was downloaded.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL from which the file was downloaded.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The download type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The download type ID. The values correspond to the five permitted values of the ZoneId property in the Mark of the Web metadata of a downloaded file on Windows. Note however that each numeric value is 1 greater than its ZoneId equivalent.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The file's download type is unknown.

1.caption: Local Machine
1.description: The file was downloaded from a server running on device.

2.caption: Intranet
2.description: The file was downloaded from an intranet server.

3.caption: Trusted
3.description: The file was downloaded from a trusted server.

4.caption: Internet
4.description: The file was downloaded from an internet server.

5.caption: Untrusted
5.description: The file was downloaded from an untrusted server.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The file's download type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

edge.Name: edge
edge.Caption: Edge
edge.Description: Represents a connection or relationship between two nodes in a graph.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the edge such as weight, distance, or custom properties.

is_directed.caption: Directed
is_directed.description: Indicates whether the edge is (true) or undirected (false).

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to this edge. Labels can be used to categorize, filter, and group edges within a graph.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The human-readable name or label for the edge.

relation.caption: Relation
relation.description: The type of relationship between nodes (e.g. is-attached-to , depends-on, etc).

source.caption: Source
source.description: The unique identifier of the node where the edge originates.

target.caption: Target
target.description: The unique identifier of the node where the edge terminates.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of the edge.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

email.Name: email
email.Caption: Email
email.Description: The Email object describes the email metadata such as sender, recipients, and direction, and can include embedded URLs and files.

bcc.caption: Bcc
bcc.description: The machine-readable email header Bcc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

bcc_mailboxes.caption: Bcc Mailboxes
bcc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Bcc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

cc.caption: Cc
cc.description: The machine-readable email header Cc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

cc_mailboxes.caption: Cc Mailboxes
cc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Cc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

delivered_to.caption: Delivered To
delivered_to.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header field. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

delivered_to_list.caption: Delivered To List
delivered_to_list.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header values. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

files.caption: Files
files.description: The files embedded or attached to the email.

from.caption: From
from.description: The machine-readable email header From value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_list.caption: From List
from_list.description: The machine-readable email header From values. This array should contain the value in from. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_mailbox.caption: From Mailbox
from_mailbox.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox value. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

from_mailboxes.caption: From Mailboxes
from_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox values. This array should contain the value in from_mailbox. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

is_read.caption: Read
is_read.description: The indication of whether the email has been read.

message_uid.caption: Message UID
message_uid.description: The email header Message-ID value, as defined by RFC 5322.

reply_to.caption: Reply To
reply_to.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_list.caption: Reply To List
reply_to_list.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_mailboxes.caption: Reply To Mailboxes
reply_to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Reply To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

return_path.caption: Return Path
return_path.description: The address found in the 'Return-Path' header, which indicates where bounce messages (non-delivery reports) should be sent. This address is often set by the sending system and may differ from the 'From' or 'Sender' addresses. For example, mailer-daemon@senderserver.com.

sender.caption: Sender
sender.description: The machine readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from field, which shows the message author. The sender field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_list field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

sender_mailbox.caption: Sender Mailbox
sender_mailbox.description: The human readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from_mailbox field, which shows the message author. The sender mailbox field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_mailboxes field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes of the email, including attachments.

smtp_from.caption: SMTP From
smtp_from.description: The value of the SMTP MAIL FROM command.

smtp_to.caption: SMTP To
smtp_to.description: The value of the SMTP envelope RCPT TO command.

subject.caption: Subject
subject.description: The email header Subject value, as defined by RFC 5322.

to.caption: To
to.description: The machine-readable email header To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

to_mailboxes.caption: To Mailboxes
to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

uid.caption: Email Thread UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the email thread.

urls.caption: URLs
urls.description: The URLs embedded in the email.

x_originating_ip.caption: X-Originating-IP
x_originating_ip.description: The X-Originating-IP header identifying the emails originating IP address(es).

email_auth.Name: email_auth
email_auth.Caption: Email Authentication
email_auth.Description: The Email Authentication object describes the Sender Policy Framework (SPF), DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) and Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) attributes of an email.

dkim.caption: DKIM Status
dkim.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) status of the email.

dkim_domain.caption: DKIM Domain
dkim_domain.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signing domain of the email.

dkim_signature.caption: DKIM Signature
dkim_signature.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signature used by the sending/receiving system.

dmarc.caption: DMARC Status
dmarc.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) status of the email.

dmarc_override.caption: DMARC Override
dmarc_override.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) override action.

dmarc_policy.caption: DMARC Policy
dmarc_policy.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) policy status.

spf.caption: SPF Status
spf.description: The Sender Policy Framework (SPF) status of the email.

encryption_details.Name: encryption_details
encryption_details.Caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.Description: Details about the encryption methodology utilized.

algorithm.caption: Encryption Algorithm
algorithm.description: The encryption algorithm used, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id

1.caption: DES
1.description: Data Encryption Standard Algorithm

2.caption: TripleDES
2.description: Triple Data Encryption Standard Algorithm

3.caption: AES
3.description: Advanced Encryption Standard Algorithm.

4.caption: RSA
4.description: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman Algorithm

5.caption: ECC
5.description: Elliptic Curve Cryptography Algorithm

6.caption: SM2
6.description: ShangMi Cryptographic Algorithm

99.caption: Other
99.description: The algorithm is not mapped. See the algorithm attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

key_length.caption: Encryption Key Length
key_length.description: The length of the encryption key used.

key_uid.caption: Key UID
key_uid.description: The unique identifier of the key used for encryption. For example, AWS KMS Key ARN.

type.caption: Encryption Type
type.description: The type of the encryption used.

endpoint.Name: endpoint
endpoint.Caption: Endpoint
endpoint.Description: The Endpoint object describes a physical or virtual device that connects to and exchanges information with a computer network. Some examples of endpoints are mobile devices, desktop computers, virtual machines, embedded devices, and servers. Internet-of-Things devices—like cameras, lighting, refrigerators, security systems, smart speakers, and thermostats—are also endpoints.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The endpoint type ID.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

endpoint_connection.Name: endpoint_connection
endpoint_connection.Caption: Endpoint Connection
endpoint_connection.Description: The Endpoint Connection object contains information detailing a connection attempt to an endpoint.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: A numerical response status code providing details about the connection.

network_endpoint.caption: Network Endpoint
network_endpoint.description: Provides characteristics of the network endpoint.

enrichment.Name: enrichment
enrichment.Caption: Enrichment
enrichment.Description: The Enrichment object provides inline enrichment data for specific attributes of interest within an event. It serves as a mechanism to enhance or supplement the information associated with the event by adding additional relevant details or context.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The enrichment data associated with the attribute and value. The meaning of this data depends on the type the enrichment record.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A long description of the enrichment data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: The reputation of the enrichment data.

short_desc.caption: Short Description
short_desc.description: A short description of the enrichment data.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL of the source of the enrichment data.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The enrichment type. For example: location.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the environment variable.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the environment variable.

epss.Name: epss
epss.Caption: EPSS
epss.Description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the EPSS score was calculated.

percentile.caption: EPSS Percentile
percentile.description: The EPSS score's percentile representing relative importance and ranking of the score in the larger EPSS dataset.

score.caption: EPPS Score
score.description: The EPSS score representing the probability [0-1] of exploitation in the wild in the next 30 days (following score publication).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the EPSS model used to calculate the score.

evidences.Name: evidences
evidences.Caption: Evidence Artifacts
evidences.Description: A collection of evidence artifacts associated to the activity/activities that triggered a security detection.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: Describes details about the user/role/process that was the source of the activity that triggered the detection.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: Describes details about an AI agent associated with the activity that triggered the detection, whether the agent performed the activity, was its target, or was otherwise involved. Use a separate evidences entry per agent when a finding involves more than one, such as an agent spawning a sub-agent in violation of usage policy.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about the API call associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

connection_info.caption: Connection Info
connection_info.description: Describes details about the network connection associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

container.caption: Container
container.description: Describes details about the container associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional evidence data that is not accounted for in the specific evidence attributes. Use only when absolutely necessary.

database.caption: Database
