database.description: Describes details about the database associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

databucket.caption: Databucket
databucket.description: Describes details about the databucket associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

device.caption: Device
device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: Describes details about the destination of the network activity that triggered the detection.

email.caption: Email
email.description: The email object associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

file.caption: File
file.description: Describes details about the file associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Describes details about the http request associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Describes details about the http response associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

ja4_fingerprint_list.caption: JA4+ Fingerprints
ja4_fingerprint_list.description: Describes details about the JA4+ fingerprints that triggered the detection.

job.caption: Job
job.description: Describes details about the scheduled job that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The naming convention or type identifier of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, the @odata.type from Microsoft Graph Alerts V2 or display_name from CrowdStrike Falcon Incident Behaviors.

process.caption: Process
process.description: Describes details about the process associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

query.caption: DNS Query
query.description: Describes details about the DNS query associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

reg_key.caption: Registry Key
reg_key.description: Describes details about the registry key that triggered the detection.

reg_value.caption: Registry Value
reg_value.description: Describes details about the registry value that triggered the detection.

resources.caption: Cloud Resources
resources.description: Describes details about the cloud resources directly related to activity that triggered the detection. For resources impacted by the detection, use Affected Resources at the top-level of the finding.

script.caption: Script
script.description: Describes details about the script that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Describes details about the source of the network activity that triggered the detection.

tls.caption: TLS
tls.description: Describes details about the Transport Layer Security (TLS) activity that triggered the detection.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, the activity_id from CrowdStrike Falcon Alerts or behavior_id from CrowdStrike Falcon Incident Behaviors.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL object that pertains to the event or object associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

user.caption: User
user.description: Describes details about the user that was the target or somehow else associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

verdict.caption: Verdict
verdict.description: The normalized verdict of the evidence associated with the security detection.

verdict_id.caption: Verdict ID
verdict_id.description: The normalized verdict (or status) ID of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, Microsoft Graph Security Alerts contain a verdict enumeration for each type of evidence associated with the Alert. This is typically set by an automated investigation process or an analyst/investigator assigned to the finding.

1.caption: False Positive
1.description: The verdict for the evidence has been identified as a False Positive.

10.caption: Duplicate
10.description: This evidence duplicates existing evidence related to this finding.

2.caption: True Positive
2.description: The verdict for the evidence has been identified as a True Positive.

3.caption: Disregard
3.description: The verdict for the evidence is that is should be Disregarded.

4.caption: Suspicious
4.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as Suspicious.

5.caption: Benign
5.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as Benign.

6.caption: Test
6.description: The evidence is part of a Test, or other sanctioned behavior(s).

7.caption: Insufficient Data
7.description: There is insufficient data to render a verdict on the evidence.

8.caption: Security Risk
8.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as a Security Risk.

9.caption: Managed Externally
9.description: The verdict for the evidence is Managed Externally, such as in a case management tool.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

win_service.caption: Windows Service
win_service.description: Describes details about the Windows service that triggered the detection.

extension.Name: extension
extension.Caption: Schema Extension
extension.Description: The OCSF Schema Extension object provides detailed information about the schema extension used to construct the event. The schema extensions are registered in the extensions.md file.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The schema extension name. For example: dev.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The schema extension unique identifier. For example: 999.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The schema extension version. For example: 1.0.0-alpha.2.

feature.Name: feature
feature.Caption: Feature
feature.Description: The Feature object provides information about the software product feature that generated a specific event. It encompasses details related to the capabilities, components, user interface (UI) design, and performance upgrades associated with the feature.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the feature.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the feature.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the feature.

file.Name: file
file.Caption: File
file.Description: The File object represents the metadata associated with a file stored in a computer system. It encompasses information about the file itself, including its attributes, properties, and organizational details.

accessed_time.caption: Accessed Time
accessed_time.description: The time when the file was last accessed.

accessor.caption: Accessor
accessor.description: The name of the user who last accessed the object.

attributes.caption: Attributes
attributes.description: The bitmask value that represents the file attributes.

company_name.caption: Company Name
company_name.description: The name of the company that published the file. For example: Microsoft Corporation.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the file was created.

creator.caption: Creator
creator.description: The user that created the file.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the file, as returned by file system. For example: the description as returned by the Unix file command or the Windows file type.

download_info.caption: Download Info
download_info.description: Information pertaining to a downloaded file.

drive_type.caption: Drive Type
drive_type.description: The drive type, normalized to the caption of the drive_type_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

drive_type_id.caption: Drive Type ID
drive_type_id.description: Identifies the type of a disk drive, i.e. fixed, removable, etc.

1.caption: Removable
1.description: The drive has removable media; for example, a floppy drive, thumb drive, or flash card reader.

2.caption: Fixed
2.description: The drive has fixed media; for example, a hard disk drive or flash drive.

3.caption: Remote
3.description: The drive is a remote (network) drive.

4.caption: CD-ROM
4.description: The drive is a CD-ROM drive.

5.caption: RAM Disk
5.description: The drive is a RAM disk.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The drive type is not mapped. See the drive_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the file. Should be populated if the file is encrypted.

ext.caption: File Extension
ext.description: The extension of the file, excluding the leading dot. For example: exe from svchost.exe, or gz from export.tar.gz.

imported_symbols.caption: Imported Symbols
imported_symbols.description: A list of symbols imported by the executable file.

internal_name.caption: Internal Name
internal_name.description: The name of the file as identified within the file itself. This contrasts with the name by which the file is known on disk. Where available, the internal name is widely used by security practitioners and detection content because the on-disk file name is not reliable. On the Windows OS, most PE files contain a VERSIONINFO resource from which the internal name can be obtained. On macOS, binaries can optionally embed a copy of the application's Info.plist file which in turn contains the name of the executable.

is_deleted.caption: Deleted
is_deleted.description: Indicates if the file was deleted from the filesystem.

is_encrypted.caption: Encrypted
is_encrypted.description: Indicates if the file is encrypted.

is_public.caption: Public
is_public.description: Indicates if the file is publicly accessible. For example in an object's public access in AWS S3

is_readonly.caption: Read-Only
is_readonly.description: Indicates that the file cannot be modified.

is_system.caption: System
is_system.description: The indication of whether the object is part of the operating system.

mime_type.caption: MIME type
mime_type.description: The Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type of the file, if applicable.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the file was last modified.

modifier.caption: Modifier
modifier.description: The user that last modified the file.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the file. For example: svchost.exe

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The user that owns the file/object.

parent_folder.caption: Parent Folder
parent_folder.description: The parent folder in which the file resides. For example: c:\windows\system32

path.caption: Path
path.description: The full path to the file. For example: c:\windows\system32\svchost.exe.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that created or installed the file.

signature.caption: Digital Signature
signature.description: The digital signature of the file.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of data, in bytes.

storage_class.caption: Storage Class
storage_class.description: The storage class of the file. For example in AWS S3: STANDARD, STANDARD_IA, GLACIER.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the file.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The file type.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The file type ID. Note the distinction between a Regular File and an Executable File. If the distinction is not known, or not indicated by the log, use Regular File. In this case, it should not be assumed that a Regular File is not executable.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the file as defined by the storage system, such the file system file ID.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

uri.caption: File URI
uri.description: The file URI, such as those reporting by static analysis tools. E.g., file:///C:/dev/sarif/sarif-tutorials/samples/Introduction/simple-example.js

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL of the file, when applicable.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The file version. For example: 8.0.7601.17514.

volume.caption: Volume
volume.description: The volume on the storage device where the file is located.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description:
An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs where each pair represents a file or folder extended attribute.

For example: Windows alternate data stream attributes (ADS stream name, ADS size, etc.), user-defined or application-defined attributes, ACL, owner, primary group, etc. Examples from DCS:

  • ads_name
  • ads_size
  • dacl
  • owner
  • primary_group
  • link_name - name of the link associated to the file.
  • hard_link_count - the number of links that are associated to the file.

finding.Name: finding
finding.Caption: Finding
finding.Description: The Finding object describes metadata related to a security finding generated by a security tool or system.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the finding was created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the reported finding.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The time when the finding was first observed.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The time when the finding was most recently observed.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the finding was last modified.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the product that reported the finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the finding.

related_events.caption: Related Events/Findings
related_events.description: Describes events and/or other findings related to the finding as identified by the security product. Note that these events may or may not be in OCSF.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL pointing to the source of the finding.

supporting_data.caption: Supporting Data
supporting_data.description: Additional data supporting a finding as provided by security tool

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the reported finding.

types.caption: Types
types.description: One or more types of the reported finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the reported finding.

finding_info.Name: finding_info
finding_info.Caption: Finding Information
finding_info.Description: The Finding Information object describes metadata related to a security finding generated by a security tool or system.

analytic.caption: Analytic
analytic.description: The analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the finding or conclusion.

attack_graph.caption: Attack Graph
attack_graph.description: An Attack Graph describes possible routes an attacker could take through an environment. It describes relationships between resources and their findings, such as malware detections, vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and other security actions.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of attack objects, each describing a tactic, technique, and/or sub-technique associated with the finding.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the finding was created.

data_sources.caption: Data Sources
data_sources.description: A list of data sources utilized in generation of the finding.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the reported finding.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was first observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was first observed.

It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: The Kill Chain provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was most recently observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was most recently observed.

It can differ from the modified_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was last modified.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the finding was last modified.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the product that reported the finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the finding.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Other analytics related to this finding.

related_events.caption: Related Events/Findings
related_events.description: Describes events and/or other findings related to the finding as identified by the security product. Note that these events may or may not be in OCSF.

related_events_count.caption: Related Events/Findings Count
related_events_count.description: Number of related events or findings.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL pointing to the source of the finding.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated with the finding.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the reported finding.

traits.caption: Traits
traits.description: The list of key traits or characteristics extracted from the finding.

types.caption: Types
types.description: One or more types of the reported finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the reported finding.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the reported finding.

fingerprint.Name: fingerprint
fingerprint.Caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.Description: The Fingerprint object provides detailed information about a fingerprint, which is a compact representation of data used to identify a longer piece of information, such as a public key, file content, or application implementation. It contains the algorithm or scheme and value of the fingerprint, enabling efficient and reliable identification of the associated data.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The algorithm or scheme used to create the fingerprint, normalized to the caption of algorithm_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized algorithm or scheme, which was used to create the fingerprint.

1.caption: MD5
1.description: MD5 message-digest algorithm producing a 128-bit (16-byte) hash value.

10.caption: SHA-512/224
10.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value truncated to a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

11.caption: SHA-512/256
11.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value truncated to a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

12.caption: SHA3-224
12.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

13.caption: SHA3-256
13.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

14.caption: SHA3-384
14.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 384-bit (48-byte) hash value.

15.caption: SHA3-512
15.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value.

16.caption: xxHash H3 64-bit
16.description: xxHash H3 producing a 64-bit hash value.

17.caption: xxHash H3 128-bit
17.description: xxHash H3 producing a 128-bit hash value.

18.caption: Imphash
18.description: Import hash (imphash) based on the import table of a Portable Executable (PE) file producing a 128-bit (16-byte) hash value.

19.caption: NPF
19.description: Network Protocol Fingerprint (NPF) used to identify network protocols and applications.

2.caption: SHA-1
2.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 1 producing a 160-bit (20-byte) hash value.

20.caption: HASSH
20.description: HASSH is a network fingerprinting standard which can be used to identify specific SSH client and server implementations.

3.caption: SHA-256
3.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

4.caption: SHA-512
4.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value.

5.caption: CTPH
5.description: The ssdeep generated fuzzy checksum. Also known as Context Triggered Piecewise Hash (CTPH).

6.caption: TLSH
6.description: The TLSH fuzzy hashing algorithm.

7.caption: quickXorHash
7.description: Microsoft simple non-cryptographic hash algorithm that works by XORing the bytes in a circular-shifting fashion.

8.caption: SHA-224
8.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

9.caption: SHA-384
9.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 384-bit (48-byte) hash value.

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The encoding of the value attribute, normalized to the caption of encoding_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding used to represent the fingerprint bytes as the string in value. A verifier must decode value using this encoding to recover the raw hash bytes.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The encoding of the fingerprint value is not known.

1.caption: Hex
1.description: The fingerprint value is encoded as a lowercase or uppercase hexadecimal string.

2.caption: Base64
2.description: The fingerprint value is encoded using standard Base64.

3.caption: Base64URL
3.description: The fingerprint value is encoded using URL- and filename-safe Base64.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The encoding of the fingerprint value is not mapped. See the encoding attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

serialization.caption: Serialization
serialization.description: The canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

serialization_id.caption: Serialization ID
serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the fingerprinted input. Use Flat where the fingerprinted data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were hashed.

1.caption: Flat
1.description: No canonical serialization was applied; the fingerprint is computed over the data's raw byte sequence, such as the content of a disk file or any other opaque byte stream.

2.caption: JCS
2.description: JSON Canonicalization Scheme - deterministic JSON serialization of the structured data prior to hashing.

3.caption: JWS
3.description: JSON Web Signature - the JWS Signing Input, i.e. BASE64URL(protected header) '.' BASE64URL(payload).

4.caption: COSE
4.description: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption - the CBOR Sig_structure used as the binary input.

5.caption: DSSE
5.description: Dead Simple Signing Envelope - the PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) canonical input. Note: DSSE is a signing-envelope scheme, not a hash algorithm; the hash algorithm is carried in algorithm_id.

6.caption: Authenticode
6.description: The Portable Executable (PE) Image Hash procedure that canonicalizes the PE structure into the byte sequence fed to the digest, excluding specified header fields and digesting sections in a defined order.

7.caption: Code Signing
7.description: The procedure that describes how hashes of code and other structures form the Code Directory message that is digested.

8.caption: App Package
8.description: The Windows Application Package signing procedure that describes how file hashes are stored in the manifest, and how that manifest is signed.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The fingerprint value.

Note: This uses type file_hash_t ("Hash"), which has been generalized for all fingerprints but retains the same name and caption for backwards compatibility.

firewall_rule.Name: firewall_rule
firewall_rule.Caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.Description: The Firewall Rule object represents a specific rule within a firewall policy or event. It contains information about a rule's configuration, properties, and associated actions that define how network traffic is handled by the firewall.

condition.caption: Condition
condition.description: The rule trigger condition for the rule. For example: SQL_INJECTION.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The rule response time duration, usually used for challenge completion time.

match_details.caption: Match Details
match_details.description: The data in a request that rule matched. For example: '["10","and","1"]'.

match_location.caption: Match Location
match_location.description: The location of the matched data in the source which resulted in the triggered firewall rule. For example: HEADER.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: The rate limit for a rate-based rule.

sensitivity.caption: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: The sensitivity of the firewall rule in the matched event. For example: HIGH.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The rule type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The rule version. For example: 1.1.

function_invocation.Name: function_invocation
function_invocation.Caption: Function Invocation
function_invocation.Description: The Function Invocation object provides details regarding the invocation of a function.

error.caption: Error Code
error.description: The error indication returned from the function. This may differ from the return value (e.g. when errno is used).

parameters.caption: Parameters
parameters.description: The parameters passed into a function invocation.

return_value.caption: Return Value
return_value.description: The value returned from a function.

gpu_info.Name: gpu_info
gpu_info.Caption: GPU Information
gpu_info.Description: The GPU information object contains attributes describing graphical processing hardware.

bus_type.caption: Bus Type
bus_type.description: The attachment bus or interface standard, normalized to the caption of the bus_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

bus_type_id.caption: Bus Type ID
bus_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the attachment bus or interface standard.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the GPU. For example: GeForce RTX A6000, Radeon PRO W7900, or Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the GPU. For example: NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel.

vram_mode.caption: VRAM Mode
vram_mode.description: The video memory attachment mode, indicating how the VRAM hardware is integrated with the system (e.g., shared or dedicated), normalized to the caption of the vram_mode_id value. For 'Other', the exact attachment mode is defined by the event source.

vram_mode_id.caption: VRAM Mode ID
vram_mode_id.description: The normalized identifier of the video memory attachment mode.

vram_size.caption: VRAM Size
vram_size.description: The total amount of installed video RAM.

graph.Name: graph
graph.Caption: Graph
graph.Description: A graph data structure representation with nodes and edges.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The graph description - provides additional details about the graph's purpose and contents.

edges.caption: Edges
edges.description: The edges/connections between nodes in the graph - contains the collection of edge objects defining relationships between nodes.

is_directed.caption: Directed
is_directed.description: Indicates if the graph is directed (true) or undirected (false).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The graph name - a human readable identifier for the graph.

nodes.caption: Nodes
nodes.description: The nodes/vertices of the graph - contains the collection of node objects that make up the graph.

query_language.caption: Query Language
query_language.description: The graph query language, normalized to the caption of the query_language_id value.

query_language_id.caption: Query Language ID
query_language_id.description: The normalized identifier of a graph query language that can be used to interact with the graph.

1.caption: Cypher
1.description: A declarative graph query language developed by Neo4j that allows for expressive and efficient querying of graph databases.

2.caption: GraphQL
2.description: A query language for APIs that enables declarative data fetching and provides a complete description of the data in the API.

3.caption: Gremlin
3.description: A graph traversal language and virtual machine developed by Apache TinkerPop that enables graph computing across different graph databases.

4.caption: GQL
4.description: An ISO standard graph query language designed to provide a unified way to query graph databases.

5.caption: G-CORE
5.description: A graph query language that combines features from existing languages while adding support for paths as first-class citizens.

6.caption: PGQL
6.description: Property Graph Query Language developed by Oracle that provides SQL-like syntax for querying property graphs.

7.caption: SPARQL
7.description: A semantic query language for databases that enables querying and manipulating data stored in RDF format.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Query Language is not mapped. See the query_language attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The graph type. Typically useful to represent the specific type of graph that is used.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of the graph - a unique ID to reference this specific graph.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

group.Name: group
group.Caption: Group
group.Description: The Group object represents a collection or association of entities, such as users, policies, or devices. It serves as a logical grouping mechanism to organize and manage entities with similar characteristics or permissions within a system or organization, including but not limited to purposes of access control.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The group description.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the group is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The group name.

type.caption: Group Type
type.description: The type of the group.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the group. For example, for Windows events this is the security identifier (SID) of the group. Another example, pool id or desktop id that the device belongs to.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

hassh.Name: hassh
hassh.Caption: HASSH
hassh.Description: The HASSH object contains SSH network fingerprinting values for specific client/server implementations. It provides a standardized way of identifying and categorizing SSH connections based on their unique characteristics and behavior.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The concatenation of key exchange, encryption, authentication and compression algorithms (separated by ';'). NOTE: This is not the underlying algorithm for the hash implementation.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The hash of the key exchange, encryption, authentication and compression algorithms.

http_cookie.Name: http_cookie
http_cookie.Caption: HTTP Cookie
http_cookie.Description: The HTTP Cookie object, also known as a web cookie or browser cookie, contains details and values pertaining to a small piece of data that a server sends to a user's web browser. This data is then stored by the browser and sent back to the server with subsequent requests, allowing the server to remember and track certain information about the user's browsing session or preferences.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain name for the server from which the http_cookie is served.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the HTTP cookie.

http_only.caption: HTTP Only
http_only.description: A cookie attribute to make it inaccessible via JavaScript

is_http_only.caption: HTTP Only
is_http_only.description: This attribute prevents the cookie from being accessed via JavaScript.

is_secure.caption: Secure
is_secure.description: The cookie attribute indicates that cookies are sent to the server only when the request is encrypted using the HTTPS protocol.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The HTTP cookie name.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The path of the HTTP cookie.

samesite.caption: SameSite
samesite.description: The cookie attribute that lets servers specify whether/when cookies are sent with cross-site requests. Values are: Strict, Lax or None

secure.caption: Secure
secure.description: The cookie attribute to only send cookies to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol.

http_header.Name: http_header
http_header.Caption: HTTP Header
http_header.Description: The HTTP Header object represents the headers sent in an HTTP request or response. HTTP headers are key-value pairs that convey additional information about the HTTP message, including details about the content, caching, authentication, encoding, and other aspects of the communication.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the HTTP header.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the HTTP header.

http_request.Name: http_request
http_request.Caption: HTTP Request
http_request.Description: The HTTP Request object represents the attributes of a request made to a web server. It encapsulates the details and metadata associated with an HTTP request, including the request method, headers, URL, query parameters, body content, and other relevant information.

args.caption: HTTP Arguments
args.description: The arguments sent along with the HTTP request.

body_length.caption: Request Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP request body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

http_method.caption: HTTP Method
http_method.description: The HTTP request method indicates the desired action to be performed for a given resource.

ACL.caption: ACL
ACL.description: The ACL method modifies the access control list of the specified resource.

BASELINE-CONTROL.caption: Baseline Control
BASELINE-CONTROL.description: The BASELINE-CONTROL method places the specified collection resource under baseline control.

BIND.caption: Bind
BIND.description: The BIND method adds a binding to the specified collection resource.

CHECKIN.caption: Check In
CHECKIN.description: The CHECKIN method creates a new version from a checked-out version-controlled resource.

CHECKOUT.caption: Check Out
CHECKOUT.description: The CHECKOUT method prepares a version-controlled resource for modification.

CONNECT.caption: Connect
CONNECT.description: The CONNECT method establishes a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource.

COPY.caption: Copy
COPY.description: The COPY method duplicates the specified resource.

DELETE.caption: Delete
DELETE.description: The DELETE method deletes the specified resource.

GET.caption: Get
GET.description: The GET method requests a representation of the specified resource. Requests using GET should only retrieve data.

HEAD.caption: Head
HEAD.description: The HEAD method asks for a response identical to a GET request, but without the response body.

LABEL.caption: Label
LABEL.description: The LABEL method adds, sets, or removes labels on a version-controlled resource.

LINK.caption: Link
LINK.description: The LINK method establishes one or more links between resources.

LOCK.caption: Lock
LOCK.description: The LOCK method acquires or refreshes a lock on the specified resource.

MERGE.caption: Merge
MERGE.description: The MERGE method merges changes from another resource into the specified resource.

MKACTIVITY.caption: Make Activity
MKACTIVITY.description: The MKACTIVITY method creates a new activity resource.

MKCALENDAR.caption: Make Calendar
MKCALENDAR.description: The MKCALENDAR method creates a new calendar collection resource.

MKCOL.caption: Make Collection
MKCOL.description: The MKCOL method creates a new collection resource.

MKREDIRECTREF.caption: Make Redirect Reference
MKREDIRECTREF.description: The MKREDIRECTREF method creates a new redirect reference resource.

MKWORKSPACE.caption: Make Workspace
MKWORKSPACE.description: The MKWORKSPACE method creates a new workspace resource.

MOVE.caption: Move
MOVE.description: The MOVE method atomically duplicates and deletes the specified resource.

OPTIONS.caption: Options
OPTIONS.description: The OPTIONS method describes the communication options for the target resource.

ORDERPATCH.caption: Order Patch
ORDERPATCH.description: The ORDERPATCH method changes the ordering of members in an ordered collection.

PATCH.caption: Patch
PATCH.description: The PATCH method applies partial modifications to a resource.

POST.caption: Post
POST.description: The POST method submits an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.

PRI.caption: PRI
PRI.description: The PRI method appears in the HTTP/2 connection preface to confirm the protocol.

PROPFIND.caption: Property Find
PROPFIND.description: The PROPFIND method retrieves properties defined on the specified resource.

PROPPATCH.caption: Property Patch
PROPPATCH.description: The PROPPATCH method sets and/or removes properties defined on the specified resource.

PUT.caption: Put
PUT.description: The PUT method replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.

QUERY.caption: Query
QUERY.description: The QUERY method performs a safe query request that can include a request body.

REBIND.caption: Rebind
REBIND.description: The REBIND method moves a binding from one collection to another.

REPORT.caption: Report
REPORT.description: The REPORT method retrieves a report about the specified resource.

SEARCH.caption: Search
SEARCH.description: The SEARCH method searches a resource or collection using the request payload.

TRACE.caption: Trace
TRACE.description: The TRACE method performs a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource.

UNBIND.caption: Unbind
UNBIND.description: The UNBIND method removes a binding from the specified collection resource.

UNCHECKOUT.caption: Un-Check Out
UNCHECKOUT.description: The UNCHECKOUT method cancels a checkout and restores the resource to its previous state.

UNLINK.caption: Unlink
UNLINK.description: The UNLINK method removes one or more links between resources.

UNLOCK.caption: Unlock
UNLOCK.description: The UNLOCK method releases a lock on the specified resource.

UPDATE.caption: Update
UPDATE.description: The UPDATE method updates a version-controlled resource to match a specified version.

UPDATEREDIRECTREF.caption: Update Redirect Reference
UPDATEREDIRECTREF.description: The UPDATEREDIRECTREF method changes the target of a redirect reference resource.

VERSION-CONTROL.caption: Version Control
VERSION-CONTROL.description: The VERSION-CONTROL method places the specified resource under version control.

length.caption: Request Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP request, in number of bytes.

referrer.caption: HTTP Referrer
referrer.description: The request header that identifies the address of the previous web page, which is linked to the current web page or resource being requested.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the http request.

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL object that pertains to the request.

user_agent.caption: HTTP User-Agent
user_agent.description: The request header that identifies the operating system and web browser.

version.caption: HTTP Version
version.description: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) version.

x_forwarded_for.caption: X-Forwarded-For
x_forwarded_for.description: The X-Forwarded-For header identifying the originating IP address(es) of a client connecting to a web server through an HTTP proxy or a load balancer.

http_response.Name: http_response
http_response.Caption: HTTP Response
http_response.Description: The HTTP Response object contains detailed information about the response sent from a web server to the requester. It encompasses attributes and metadata that describe the response status, headers, body content, and other relevant information.

body_length.caption: Response Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP response body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) status code returned from the web server to the client. For example, 200.

content_type.caption: HTTP Content Type
content_type.description: The HTTP request header that identifies the original media type of the resource (prior to any content encoding applied for sending).

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

latency.caption: Latency
latency.description: The HTTP response latency measured in milliseconds.

length.caption: Response Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP response, in number of bytes.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The HTTP status code and reason phrase returned from the server.

@deprecated.message: Redundant with the code and status attributes, which together convey the HTTP status code and its reason phrase. Use code for the numeric value and status for the human-readable label.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The response status. For example: A successful HTTP status of 'OK' which corresponds to a code of 200.

iam_role.Name: iam_role
iam_role.Caption: IAM Role
iam_role.Description: The IAM Role object describes permission characteristics (or privileges) associated with a user or group of users as security principals against one or more resources. In some cases only the name or ID of the role is known hence other attributes are optional. In some systems a user or group of users can have multiple roles, imparting the union of privileges to the principal. In some systems the role can serve as a temporary security principal without its own credentials on behalf of the actual security principal.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The account associated with the role. For example, can be a cross-account role, different from the user or group account, granting access within this account.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The role name. For example, Power Users.

policies.caption: Policies
policies.description: IAM policies associated with the role.

privileges.caption: Privileges
privileges.description: List of privileges assigned to a role.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated with the role.

resources.caption: Resources Array
resources.description: Resources that the role applies to.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The session where the role is active. Some roles may be temporary and expire when the session expires.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique role identifier. For example, the Windows role SID, or AWS role ARN.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory role GUID or the associated LDAP group DN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

identity_activity_metrics.Name: identity_activity_metrics
identity_activity_metrics.Caption: Identity Activity Metrics
identity_activity_metrics.Description: The Identity Activity Metrics object captures usage patterns, authentication activity, credential usage and other metrics for identities across cloud and on-premises environments. Example identities include AWS IAM Users, Roles, Azure AD Principals, GCP Service Accounts, on-premises Active Directory accounts.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The timestamp when this identity was first observed or created in the system. This helps establish the identity's age and lifecycle stage for risk assessment.

last_authentication_time.caption: Last Authentication Time
last_authentication_time.description: The timestamp when this identity last successfully authenticated to any system or service. This differs from last_seen_time as it specifically tracks authentication events rather than all activities.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The timestamp of the most recent activity performed by this identity, including authentication, resource access, or API calls. This is the most comprehensive indicator of identity usage recency.

password_last_used_time.caption: Password Last Used Time
password_last_used_time.description: The timestamp when password-based authentication was last used by this identity. This helps distinguish between password and other authentication methods (MFA, SSO, certificates) and identify password-specific usage patterns.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Details about the programmatic credentials associated with this identity, such as API keys, service account keys, access tokens, and client certificates used for automated access.

idp.Name: idp
idp.Caption: Identity Provider
idp.Description: The Identity Provider object contains detailed information about a provider responsible for creating, maintaining, and managing identity information while offering authentication services to applications. An Identity Provider (IdP) serves as a trusted authority that verifies the identity of users and issues authentication tokens or assertions to enable secure access to applications or services.

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: The Authentication Factors object describes the different types of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) methods and/or devices supported by the Identity Provider.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The primary domain associated with the Identity Provider.

fingerprint.caption: Certificate Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the X.509 certificate used by the Identity Provider.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Enforced
has_mfa.description: The Identity Provider enforces Multi Factor Authentication (MFA).

issuer.caption: Issuer Details
issuer.description: The unique identifier (often a URL) used by the Identity Provider as its issuer.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the Identity Provider.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol of the Identity Provider. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

scim.caption: SCIM
scim.description: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) resource object as defined in RFC 7634 provides a structured set of attributes related to SCIM protocols used for identity provisioning and management across cloud-based platforms. It standardizes user and group provisioning details, enabling identity synchronization and lifecycle management with compatible Identity Providers (IdPs) and applications.

sso.caption: SSO
sso.description: The Single Sign-On (SSO) object provides a structure for normalizing SSO attributes, configuration, and/or settings from Identity Providers.

state.caption: State
state.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the Identity Provider to reflect its configuration or activation status.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is unknown.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Identity Provider is in an Active state, or otherwise enabled.

2.caption: Suspended
2.description: The Identity Provider is in a Suspended state.

3.caption: Deprecated
3.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deprecated state, or is otherwise disabled.

4.caption: Deleted
4.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deleted state.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The tenant ID associated with the Identity Provider.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the Identity Provider.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: Configuration URL
url_string.description: The URL for accessing the configuration or metadata of the Identity Provider.

image.Name: image
image.Caption: Image
image.Description: The Image object provides a description of a specific Virtual Machine (VM) or Container image.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the image.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The image name. For example: elixir.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The full path to the image file.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the image.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique image ID. For example: 77af4d6b9913.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ja4_fingerprint.Name: ja4_fingerprint
ja4_fingerprint.Caption: JA4+ Fingerprint
ja4_fingerprint.Description: The JA4+ fingerprint object provides detailed fingerprint information about various aspects of network traffic which is both machine and human readable.

section_a.caption: JA4 Section A
section_a.description: The 'a' section of the JA4 fingerprint.

section_b.caption: JA4 Section B
section_b.description: The 'b' section of the JA4 fingerprint.

section_c.caption: JA4 Section C
section_c.description: The 'c' section of the JA4 fingerprint.

section_d.caption: JA4 Section D
section_d.description: The 'd' section of the JA4 fingerprint.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The JA4+ fingerprint type as defined by FoxIO, normalized to the caption of 'type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The identifier of the JA4+ fingerprint type.

1.caption: JA4
1.description: TLS Client Fingerprint.

2.caption: JA4Server
2.description: TLS Server Response/Session Fingerprint.

3.caption: JA4HTTP
3.description: HTTP Client Fingerprint.

4.caption: JA4Latency
4.description: Latency Measurement/Light Distance Fingerprint.

5.caption: JA4X509
5.description: X509 TLS Certificate Fingerprint.

6.caption: JA4SSH
6.description: SSH Traffic Fingerprint.

7.caption: JA4TCP
7.description: Passive TCP Client Fingerprint.

8.caption: JA4TCPServer
8.description: Passive TCP Server Fingerprint.

9.caption: JA4TCPScan
9.description: Active TCP Server Fingerprint.

job.Name: job
job.Caption: Job
job.Description: The Job object provides information about a scheduled job or task, including its name, command line, and state. It encompasses attributes that describe the properties and status of the scheduled job.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the job was created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the job.

file.caption: File
file.description: The file that pertains to the job.

job_actions.caption: Job Actions
job_actions.description: An array of actions that will be performed by the job when certain conditions are met.

job_triggers.caption: Job Triggers
job_triggers.description: An array of conditions or events that, when met, will initiate the job to perform specified actions.

last_run_time.caption: Last Run
last_run_time.description: The time when the job was last run.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the job.

next_run_time.caption: Next Run
next_run_time.description: The time when the job will next be run.

run_state.caption: Run State
run_state.description: The run state of the job.

run_state_id.caption: Run State ID
run_state_id.description: The run state ID of the job.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The job type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The job type, i.e. the mechanism that executes the job.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The job orchestration mechanism is unknown.

1.caption: Task Scheduler
1.description: The job is executed by the Task Scheduler on Windows.

2.caption: Cron
2.description: The job is executed by cron on Linux, macOS, or another a Unix-like OS.

3.caption: Systemd
3.description: The job is executed by systemd on Linux.

4.caption: Launchd
4.description: The job is executed by launchd on macOS.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The job orchestration mechanism is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique job identifier.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that created the job.

job_action.Name: job_action
job_action.Caption: Job Action
job_action.Description: The action that will be performed by the job when certain conditions are met.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description:
When type_id is Execute (2), this describes the command line that is executed.

When type_id is COM Handler (1), this may describe the DLL path stored in the COM component's InprocServer32 key or the command line stored in the COM component's LocalServer32 key.

com_class_uuid.caption: COM Class Identifier
com_class_uuid.description: When type_id is COM Handler (1), this describes the COM Class Identifier (CLSID).

file.caption: File
file.description: When known, describes the image file that is executed when type_id is COM Handler or Execute. Note that this attribute is intended to supplement the com_class_uid or cmd_line attributes, and is not an alternative to them.

properties.caption: Properties
properties.description:
The list of properties associated with the performed action.
Can be populated with additional attributes of a program execution process, COM object attributes, fields of a message box or an email.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The job action type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The job action type.

1.caption: COM Handler
1.description: The action fires a COM handler. When this type is used, com_class_uuid and file attributes may be populated.

2.caption: Execute
2.description: The action executes a command-line operation. When this type is used, cmd_line and file attributes may be populated.

3.caption: E-mail
3.description: The action sends an email.

4.caption: Show Message
4.description: The action shows a message box with specified message and title.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The performed action is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: When type_id is Execute (2), this describes the working directory of a program that is run by the job.

job_trigger.Name: job_trigger
job_trigger.Caption: Job Trigger
job_trigger.Description: The condition or event that, when met, will initiate the job to perform specified actions.

event_codes.caption: Event Codes
event_codes.description: Event identifiers that pertain to the job trigger. Should be populated when the Event (3) type is specified.

last_run_time.caption: Last Run
last_run_time.description: The time when the job was last run.

log_sources.caption: Log Sources
log_sources.description: A collection of log systems or components that pertain to the job trigger. Should be populated when the Event (3) type is specified.

next_run_time.caption: Next Run
next_run_time.description: The time when the job will next be run.

properties.caption: Properties
properties.description:
The list of properties associated with the trigger.
Can be used to describe time boundaries of the job, amount of repetitions or when the job should be activated or expired.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The job trigger type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The job trigger type, i.e. the condition that must be met for the job to perform its action.

1.caption: Boot
1.description: The job is triggered on a system boot.

2.caption: Schedule
2.description: The job is triggered on a specific schedule. Properties should be populated with respective time bounds.

3.caption: Event
3.description: The job is triggered when the specific event occurs. The properties attribute should be populated with respective event sources and identifiers.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The job trigger is unmapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that pertains to the job trigger. Can be populated when the Event (3) type that bounds to specific user is used.

kb_article.Name: kb_article
kb_article.Caption: KB Article
kb_article.Description: The KB Article object contains metadata that describes the patch or update.

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the kb article.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The date the kb article was released by the vendor.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the kb article.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the kb article.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The normalized install state is unknown.

1.caption: Installed
1.description: The item is installed.

2.caption: Not Installed
2.description: The item is not installed.

3.caption: Installed Pending Reboot
3.description: The item is installed pending reboot operation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The install state is not mapped. See the install_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The kb article has been replaced by another.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the kb article applies.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product details the kb article applies.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the kb article.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the kb article.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The kb article link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: The title of the kb article.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the kb article.

kernel.Name: kernel
kernel.Caption: Kernel Resource
kernel.Description: The Kernel Resource object provides information about a specific kernel resource, including its name and type. It describes essential attributes associated with a resource managed by the kernel of an operating system.

is_system.caption: System
is_system.description: The indication of whether the object is part of the operating system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the kernel resource.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The full path of the kernel resource.

system_call.caption: System Call
system_call.description: The system call that was invoked.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the kernel resource.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of the kernel resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

kernel_driver.Name: kernel_driver
kernel_driver.Caption: Kernel Extension
kernel_driver.Description: The Kernel Extension object describes a kernel driver that has been loaded or unloaded into the operating system (OS) kernel.

file.caption: File
file.description: The driver/extension file object.

key_value_object.Name: key_value_object
key_value_object.Caption: Key:Value object
key_value_object.Description: A generic object allowing to define a {key:value} pair.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the key.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value associated to the key.

values.caption: Values
values.description: Optional, the values associated to the key. You can populate this attribute, when you have multiple values for the same key.

keyboard_info.Name: keyboard_info
keyboard_info.Caption: Keyboard Information
keyboard_info.Description: The Keyboard Information object contains details and attributes related to a computer or device keyboard. It encompasses information that describes the characteristics, capabilities, and configuration of the keyboard.

function_keys.caption: Function Keys
function_keys.description: The number of function keys on client keyboard.

ime.caption: IME
ime.description: The Input Method Editor (IME) file name.

keyboard_layout.caption: Keyboard Layout
keyboard_layout.description: The keyboard locale identifier name (e.g., en-US).

kill_chain_phase.Name: kill_chain_phase
kill_chain_phase.Caption: Kill Chain Phase
kill_chain_phase.Description: The Kill Chain Phase object represents a single phase of a cyber attack, including the initial reconnaissance and planning stages up to the final objective of the attacker. It provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

phase_id.caption: Kill Chain Phase ID
phase_id.description: The cyber kill chain phase identifier.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The kill chain phase is unknown.

1.caption: Reconnaissance
1.description: The attackers pick a target and perform a detailed analysis, start collecting information (email addresses, conferences information, etc.) and evaluate the victim’s vulnerabilities to determine how to exploit them.

2.caption: Weaponization
2.description: The attackers develop a malware weapon and aim to exploit the discovered vulnerabilities.

3.caption: Delivery
3.description: The intruders will use various tactics, such as phishing, infected USB drives, etc.

4.caption: Exploitation
4.description: The intruders start leveraging vulnerabilities to executed code on the victim’s system.

5.caption: Installation
5.description: The intruders install malware on the victim’s system.

6.caption: Command & Control
6.description: Malware opens a command channel to enable the intruders to remotely manipulate the victim's system.

7.caption: Actions on Objectives
7.description: With hands-on keyboard access, intruders accomplish the mission’s goal.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The kill chain phase is not mapped. See the phase attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

ldap_person.Name: ldap_person
ldap_person.Caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.Description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.

cost_center.caption: Cost Center
cost_center.description: The cost center associated with the user.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

deleted_time.caption: Deleted Time
deleted_time.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

department.caption: Department
department.description: The name of the department in which the user works.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the LDAP person. According to RFC 2798, this is the preferred name of a person to be used when displaying entries.

email_addrs.caption: Email Addresses
email_addrs.description: A list of additional email addresses for the user.

employee_uid.caption: Employee ID
employee_uid.description: The employee identifier assigned to the user by the organization.

given_name.caption: Given Name
given_name.description: The given or first name of the user.

hire_time.caption: Hire Time
hire_time.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The labels associated with the user. For example in AD this could be the userType, employeeType. For example: Member, Employee.

last_login_time.caption: Last Login
last_login_time.description: The last time when the user logged in.

ldap_cn.caption: LDAP Common Name
ldap_cn.description: The LDAP and X.500 commonName attribute, typically the full name of the person. For example, John Doe.

ldap_dn.caption: LDAP Distinguished Name
ldap_dn.description: The X.500 Distinguished Name (DN) is a structured string that uniquely identifies an entry, such as a user, in an X.500 directory service For example, cn=John Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com.

leave_time.caption: Leave Time
leave_time.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location associated with a user. This is typically the user's usual work location.

manager.caption: Manager
manager.description: The user's manager. This helps in understanding an org hierarchy. This should only ever be populated once in an event. I.e. there should not be a manager's manager in an event.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

office_location.caption: Office Location
office_location.description: The primary office location associated with the user. This could be any string and isn't a specific address. For example, South East Virtual.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user. Corresponds to the LDAP Telephone-Number CN.

surname.caption: Surname
surname.description: The last or family name for the user.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the user.

load_balancer.Name: load_balancer
load_balancer.Caption: Load Balancer
load_balancer.Description: The load balancer object describes the load balancer entity and contains additional information regarding the distribution of traffic across a network.

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The request classification as defined by the load balancer.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The numeric response status code detailing the connection from the load balancer to the destination target.

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: The destination to which the load balancer is distributing traffic.

endpoint_connections.caption: Endpoint Connections
endpoint_connections.description: An object detailing the load balancer connection attempts and responses.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the load balancer node that handled the client request. Note: the load balancer may have other IP addresses, and this is not an IP address of the target/distribution endpoint - see dst_endpoint.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The load balancer message.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: General purpose metrics associated with the load balancer.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the load balancer.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: The status detail contains additional status information about the load balancer distribution event.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the load balancer.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

location.Name: location
location.Caption: Geo Location
location.Description: The Geo Location object describes a geographical location, usually associated with an IP address.

aerial_height.caption: Aerial Height
aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

coordinates.caption: Coordinates
coordinates.description: A two-element array, containing a longitude/latitude pair. The format conforms with GeoJSON. For example: [-73.983, 40.719].

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the geographical location.

geodetic_altitude.caption: Geodetic Altitude
geodetic_altitude.description: The aircraft distance above or below the ellipsoid as measured along a line that passes through the aircraft and is normal to the surface of the WGS-84 ellipsoid. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

geodetic_vertical_accuracy.caption: Geodetic Vertical Accuracy
geodetic_vertical_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on geodetic altitude. This is based on ADS-B Geodetic Vertical Accuracy (GVA). Measured in meters.

geohash.caption: Geohash
geohash.description:
Geohash of the geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude).

Geohashing is a geocoding system used to encode geographic coordinates in decimal degrees, to a single string.

horizontal_accuracy.caption: Horizontal Accuracy
horizontal_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal position. This is based on ADS-B NACp. Measured in meters.

is_on_premises.caption: On-Premises
is_on_premises.description: Indicates whether the location is on-premises.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

@deprecated.message: Use the network_endpoint.isp or whois.isp attribute according to your use-case.

lat.caption: Latitude
lat.description: The geographical Latitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: 42.361145.

long.caption: Longitude
long.description: The geographical Longitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: -71.057083.

postal_code.caption: Postal Code
postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

pressure_altitude.caption: Pressure Altitude
pressure_altitude.description: The uncorrected barometric pressure altitude (based on reference standard 29.92 inHg, 1013.25 mb) provides a reference for algorithms that utilize 'altitude deltas' between aircraft. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m.. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the geographical location data.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The alphanumeric code that identifies the principal subdivision (e.g. province or state) of the country. For example, 'CH-VD' for the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland

logger.Name: logger
logger.Caption: Logger
logger.Description: The Logger object represents the device and product where events are stored with times for receipt and transmission.  This may be at the source device where the event occurred, a remote scanning device, intermediate hops, or the ultimate destination.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device where the events are logged.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier of the event assigned by the logger.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

log_format.caption: Log Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log. For example JSON, syslog or CSV.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The log name for the logging provider log, or the file name of the system log. This may be an intermediate store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log. For example /archive/server1/var/log/messages.0 or /var/log/.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. This may be an intermediate application store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the logging product instance.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product logging the event.  This may be the event source product, a management server product, a scanning product, a SIEM, etc.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the logging product instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the logging provider.

long_string.Name: long_string
long_string.Caption: Long String
long_string.Description: This object is a used to capture strings which may be truncated by a security product due to their length.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates that value has been truncated. May be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The size in bytes of the string represented by value before truncation. Should be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The string value, truncated if is_truncated is true.

malware.Name: malware
malware.Caption: Malware
malware.Description: The Malware object describes the classification of known malicious software, which is intentionally designed to cause damage to a computer, server, client, or computer network.

classification_ids.caption: Classification IDs
classification_ids.description: The list of normalized identifiers of the malware classifications.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification is not mapped. See the classifications attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

classifications.caption: Classifications
