classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

cves.caption: CVE List
cves.description: The list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers associated with the malware.

files.caption: Files
files.description: The list of file objects representing files that were identified as infected by the malware.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The malware name, as reported by the detection engine.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The number of files that were identified to be infected by the malware.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The filesystem path of the malware that was observed.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name or identifier of the security solution or service that provided the malware detection information.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the malware, normalized to the captions of the severity_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the malware severity.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the specific malware instance, as assigned by the detection engine (e.g., virus signature ID or IPS rule ID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

malware_scan_info.Name: malware_scan_info
malware_scan_info.Caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.Description: The malware scan information object describes characteristics, metadata of a malware scanning job.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

num_files.caption: Scanned Files
num_files.description: The total number of files analyzed during the scan.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The total number of files identified as infected with malware during the scan.

num_volumes.caption: Number of Volumes
num_volumes.description: The total number of storage volumes examined during the malware scan.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The total size in bytes of all files that were scanned.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of scan.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

1.caption: Manual
1.description: The scan was manually initiated by the user or administrator.

2.caption: Scheduled
2.description: The scan was started based on scheduler.

3.caption: Updated Content
3.description: The scan was triggered by a content update.

4.caption: Quarantined Items
4.description: The scan was triggered by newly quarantined items.

5.caption: Attached Media
5.description: The scan was triggered by the attachment of removable media.

6.caption: User Logon
6.description: The scan was started due to a user logon.

7.caption: ELAM
7.description: The scan was triggered by an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) detection.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The scan type id is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Scan UID
uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

unique_malware_count.caption: Unique Malware Count
unique_malware_count.description: The number of unique malware detected across all infected files.

managed_entity.Name: managed_entity
managed_entity.Caption: Managed Entity
managed_entity.Description: The Managed Entity object describes the type and version of an entity, such as a user, device, or policy. For types in the type_id enum list, an associated attribute should be populated. If the type of entity is not in the type_id list, information can be put into the data attribute, type_id should be 'Other' and the type attribute should label the entity type.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The managed entity content as a JSON object.

device.caption: Device
device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The group object associated with an entity such as user, policy, or rule.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The detailed geographical location usually associated with an IP address.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the managed entity. It should match the name of the specific entity object's name if populated, or the name of the managed entity if the type_id is 'Other'.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: The Organization object containing details about the managed organizational entity. This object includes properties such as the organization name, unique identifier, type, and other organizational metadata. This attribute should be populated when type_id is 4 (Organization).

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Describes details of a managed policy.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The managed entity type. For example: Policy, User, Organization, Device.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of the Managed Entity. It is recommended to also populate the type attribute with the associated label, or the source specific name if Other.

1.caption: Device
1.description: A managed Device entity. This item corresponds to population of the device attribute.

2.caption: User
2.description: A managed User entity. This item corresponds to population of the user attribute.

3.caption: Group
3.description: A managed Group entity. This item corresponds to population of the group attribute.

4.caption: Organization
4.description: A managed Organization entity. This item corresponds to population of the org attribute.

5.caption: Policy
5.description: A managed Policy entity. This item corresponds to population of the policy attribute.

6.caption: Email
6.description: A managed Email entity. This item corresponds to population of the email attribute.

7.caption: Network Zone
7.description: A managed Network Zone entity. Populate the name attribute with the zone name and/or the uid attribute with the zone ID. Additional zone information can be added to the data attribute.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The identifier of the managed entity. It should match the uid of the specific entity's object UID if populated, or the source specific ID if the type_id is 'Other'.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that pertains to the event or object.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the managed entity. For example: 1.2.3.

message_context.Name: message_context
message_context.Caption: Message Context
message_context.Description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

ai_role_id.caption: AI Role ID
ai_role_id.description: Specifies the functional role of the AI within the context of this message, such as retrieving information, assisting reasoning, executing a tool, or generating content.

1.caption: User
1.description: The human user initiating a request.

2.caption: Assistant
2.description: The AI model generating a response.

3.caption: Tool
3.description: A callable tool or API invoked by the assistant.

4.caption: Agent
4.description: A software agent that performs tasks with autonomy or delegated intent.

5.caption: Orchestrator
5.description: The component coordinating multiple agents or tools.

6.caption: Retriever
6.description: A component that retrieves information or context from a knowledge source (e.g., vector DB, search system, or API).

99.caption: Other
99.description: Other role type not covered above.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The initiating client application. In AI systems, this represents the client-side application or framework that initiates requests (e.g., LangChain application, web browser, mobile app, SDK implementation).

completion_tokens.caption: Completion Tokens
completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the model's response/completion for this message.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name or identifier of the message context. In AI systems, this could be the conversation ID, session name, thread identifier, or interaction name (e.g., 'user-session-123', 'conversation-abc', 'chat-thread-456').

prompt_text.caption: Prompt Text
prompt_text.description: The text of the input prompt provided to the model for this message. This is the verbatim instruction, query, or context supplied to the AI system that drove the operation.

prompt_tokens.caption: Prompt Tokens
prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the input prompt for this message.

response_text.caption: Response Text
response_text.description: The text of the model's response generated for this message. For agent-mediated operations, this is the content returned by the assistant, tool, or agent.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The server or service handling the request. In AI systems, this represents the AI service, API endpoint, or agent that processes and responds to requests (e.g., OpenAI API service, Claude API service, internal AI model service).

total_tokens.caption: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used for this message (prompt + completion).

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the message context. This could be a session ID, conversation ID, or other unique identifier that allows correlation of messages within the same context.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

metadata.Name: metadata
metadata.Caption: Metadata
metadata.Description: The Metadata object describes the metadata associated with the event.

correlation_uid.caption: Correlation UID
correlation_uid.description: A unique identifier used to correlate this OCSF event with other related OCSF events, distinct from the event's uid value. This enables linking multiple OCSF events that are part of the same activity, transaction, or security incident across different systems or time periods.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

debug.caption: Debug Information
debug.description: Debug information about non-fatal issues with this OCSF event. Each issue is a line in this string array.

event_code.caption: Event Code
event_code.description: The identifier of the original event. For example the numerical Windows Event Code or Cisco syslog code.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.caption: Schema Extensions
extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to the event. For example: ["sample", "dev"]

log_format.caption: Log Source Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log where the data originated. For example CSV, XML, Windows Multiline, JSON, syslog or Cisco Log Schema.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The event log name, typically for the consumer of the event. For example, the storage bucket name, SIEM repository index name, etc.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example AWS CloudWatch or Splunk.

log_source.caption: Log Source
log_source.description: The log system or component where the data originated. For example, a file path, syslog server name or a Windows hostname and logging subsystem such as Security.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

loggers.caption: Loggers
loggers.description: An ordered array of Logger objects describing each hop in the event pipeline between the source and its final destination. Each entry captures the logging product, device, and timestamps (logged_time, transmit_time) at that stage. The last entry's logged_time should match metadata.logged_time.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_event_uid.caption: Original Event ID
original_event_uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the event in its original logging system before transformation to OCSF format. This field preserves the source system's native event identifier, enabling traceability back to the raw log entry. For example, a Windows Event Record ID, a syslog message ID, a Splunk _cd value, or a database transaction log sequence number.

original_time.caption: Original Time
original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source, preserved as a pass-through string in its native format (e.g., Syslog timestamp, Windows event time). This is not normalized to timestamp_t - the normalized equivalent is the base event time attribute. Omit if the event is generated rather than collected via logs.

processed_time.caption: Processed Time
processed_time.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.caption: Profiles
profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

reporter.caption: Reporter
reporter.description: The entity from which the event or finding was first reported.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.

source.caption: Source
source.description: The source of the event or finding. This can be any distinguishing name for the logical origin of the data — for example, 'CloudTrail Events', or a use case like 'Attack Simulations' or 'Vulnerability Scans'.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the event.

total_queued_duration.caption: Total Queued Duration
total_queued_duration.description: The amount of time an event spent in a queue awaiting processing. In this case, the value is the difference between processed_time and logged_time. This duration is inclusive of all queues between the originator of the event and the intended long-term storage destination of the event.

transformation_info_list.caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info_list.description: An array of transformation info that describes the mappings or transforms applied to the data.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the event or finding as a subset of the source of the event. This can be any distinguishing characteristic of the data. For example 'Management Events' or 'Device Penetration Test'.

uid.caption: Event UID
uid.description: A unique identifier assigned to the OCSF event. This ID is specific to the OCSF event itself and is distinct from the original event identifier in the source system (see original_event_uid).

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

metric.Name: metric
metric.Caption: Metric
metric.Description: The Metric object defines a simple name/value pair entity for a metric.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the metric.

mitigation.Name: mitigation
mitigation.Caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.Description: The MITRE Mitigation object describes the ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

countermeasures.caption: Countermeasures
countermeasures.description: The D3FEND countermeasures that are associated with the attack technique. For example: ATT&CK Technique T1003 is addressed by Mitigation M1027, and D3FEND Technique D3-OTP.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The Mitigation name that is associated with the attack technique. For example: Password Policies, or Code Signing.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the Mitigation. For example: https://attack.mitre.org/versions/v14/mitigations/M1027.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The Mitigation ID that is associated with the attack technique. For example: M1027, or AML.M0013.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

module.Name: module
module.Caption: Module
module.Description: The Module object describes the attributes of a module.

base_address.caption: Base Address
base_address.description: The memory address where the module was loaded.

file.caption: File
file.description: The module file object.

function_invocation.caption: Function Invocation
function_invocation.description: Details about the invocation of the function given in function_name.

function_name.caption: Function Name
function_name.description: The invoked function in the module. For load and unload events, this is the entry-point function of the module. The system calls the entry-point function whenever a process or thread loads or unloads the module.

load_type.caption: Load Type
load_type.description: The load type, normalized to the caption of the load_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

load_type_id.caption: Load Type ID
load_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for how the module was loaded in memory.

1.caption: Standard
1.description: A normal module loaded by the normal windows loading mechanism i.e. LoadLibrary.

2.caption: Non Standard
2.description: A module loaded in a way avoidant of normal windows procedures. i.e. Bootstrapped Loading/Manual Dll Loading.

3.caption: ShellCode
3.description: A raw module in process memory that is READWRITE_EXECUTE and had a thread started in its range.

4.caption: Mapped
4.description: A memory mapped file, typically created with CreatefileMapping/MapViewOfFile.

5.caption: NonStandard Backed
5.description: A module loaded in a non standard way. However, GetModuleFileName succeeds on this allocation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The load type is not mapped. See the load_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

start_address.caption: Start Address
start_address.description: The start address of the execution.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The module type.

network_connection_info.Name: network_connection_info
network_connection_info.Caption: Network Connection Information
network_connection_info.Description: The Network Connection Information object describes characteristics of an OSI Transport Layer communication, including TCP and UDP.

boundary.caption: Boundary
boundary.description:
The boundary of the connection, normalized to the caption of 'boundary_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary(same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

boundary_id.caption: Boundary ID
boundary_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the boundary of the connection.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary (same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

1.caption: Localhost
1.description: Local network traffic on the same endpoint.

10.caption: Gateway VPC
10.description: Through a gateway VPC endpoint (Nitro-based instances only)

11.caption: Internet Gateway
11.description: Through an Internet gateway (Nitro-based instances only)

2.caption: Internal
2.description: Internal network traffic between two endpoints inside network.

3.caption: External
3.description: External network traffic between two endpoints on the Internet or outside the network.

4.caption: Same VPC
4.description: Through another resource in the same VPC

5.caption: Internet/VPC Gateway
5.description: Through an Internet gateway or a gateway VPC endpoint

6.caption: Virtual Private Gateway
6.description: Through a virtual private gateway

7.caption: Intra-region VPC
7.description: Through an intra-region VPC peering connection

8.caption: Inter-region VPC
8.description: Through an inter-region VPC peering connection

9.caption: Local Gateway
9.description: Through a local gateway

99.caption: Other
99.description: The boundary is not mapped. See the boundary attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

community_uid.caption: Community ID
community_uid.description: The Community ID of the network connection.

direction.caption: Direction
direction.description: The direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email, normalized to the caption of the direction_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

direction_id.caption: Direction ID
direction_id.description: The normalized identifier of the direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email.

1.caption: Inbound
1.description: Inbound network connection. The connection originated from the Internet or outside network, destined for services on the inside network.

2.caption: Outbound
2.description: Outbound network connection. The connection originated from inside the network, destined for services on the Internet or outside network.

3.caption: Lateral
3.description: Lateral network connection. The connection originated from inside the network, destined for services on the inside network.

4.caption: Local
4.description: Local network connection (localhost). The connection is intra-device, originating from and destined for services running on the same device.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The direction is not mapped. See the direction attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

flag_history.caption: Connection Flag History
flag_history.description: The Connection Flag History summarizes events in a network connection. For example flags ShAD representing SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK and Data exchange.

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The authenticated user or service session.

tcp_flags.caption: TCP Flags
tcp_flags.description: The network connection TCP header flags (i.e., control bits).

uid.caption: Connection UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the connection.

network_endpoint.Name: network_endpoint
network_endpoint.Caption: Network Endpoint
network_endpoint.Description: The Network Endpoint object describes characteristics of a network endpoint. These can be a source or destination of a network connection.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: Fingerprints that identify the specific application implementation on this endpoint, such as Cisco NPF or HASSH.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

network_scope.caption: Network Scope
network_scope.description: Indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined. The value is normalized to the caption of the network_scope_id.

network_scope_id.caption: Network Scope ID
network_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the endpoint’s network scope. The normalized network scope identifier indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: Unknown whether this endpoint resides within the customer’s network.

1.caption: Internal
1.description: The endpoint resides inside the customer’s network.

2.caption: External
2.description: The endpoint is on the Internet or otherwise external to the customer’s network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The network scope is not mapped. See the network_scope attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

port.caption: Port
port.description: The port used for communication within the network connection.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The network proxy information pertaining to a specific endpoint. This can be used to describe information pertaining to network address translation (NAT).

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network endpoint type ID.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

network_interface.Name: network_interface
network_interface.Caption: Network Interface
network_interface.Description: The Network Interface object describes the type and associated attributes of a physical or virtual network interface.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname associated with the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address associated with the network interface.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The MAC address of the network interface.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the network interface.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful in merger or acquisition situations. For example, when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

open_ports.caption: Open Ports
open_ports.description: The list of open ports on a network interface, including port numbers and associated protocol information.

subnet_prefix.caption: Subnet Prefix Length
subnet_prefix.description: The subnet prefix length determines the number of bits used to represent the network part of the IP address. The remaining bits are reserved for identifying individual hosts within that subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of network interface.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network interface type identifier.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the network interface.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

network_proxy.Name: network_proxy
network_proxy.Caption: Network Proxy Endpoint
network_proxy.Description: The network proxy endpoint object describes a proxy server, which acts as an intermediary between a client requesting a resource and the server providing that resource.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

network_traffic.Name: network_traffic
network_traffic.Caption: Network Traffic
network_traffic.Description: The Network Traffic object describes characteristics of network traffic over a time period. The metrics represent network data transferred between source and destination during an observation window.

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The total number of bytes transferred in both directions (sum of bytes_in and bytes_out).

bytes_in.caption: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: The number of bytes sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

bytes_missed.caption: Bytes Missed
bytes_missed.description: The number of bytes that were missed during observation, typically due to packet loss or sampling limitations.

bytes_out.caption: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: The number of bytes sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

chunks.caption: Chunks
chunks.description: The total number of chunks transferred in both directions (sum of chunks_in and chunks_out).

chunks_in.caption: Chunks In
chunks_in.description: The number of chunks sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

chunks_out.caption: Chunks Out
chunks_out.description: The number of chunks sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end time of the observation or reporting period.

packets.caption: Total Packets
packets.description: The total number of packets transferred in both directions (sum of packets_in and packets_out).

packets_in.caption: Packets In
packets_in.description: The number of packets sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

packets_out.caption: Packets Out
packets_out.description: The number of packets sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start time of the observation or reporting period.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time span object representing the duration of the observation or reporting period.

node.Name: node
node.Caption: Node
node.Description: Represents a node or a vertex in a graph structure.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the node stored as key-value pairs. Can include custom properties specific to the node.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A human-readable description of the node's purpose or meaning in the graph.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to this node. Labels can be used to categorize, filter, and group nodes within a graph.

name.caption: Name
name.description: A human-readable name or label for the node. Should be descriptive and unique within the graph context.

type.caption: Type
type.description: Categorizes the node into a specific class or type. Useful for grouping and filtering nodes.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique string or numeric identifier that distinguishes this node from all others in the graph. Must be unique across all nodes.

note.Name: note
note.Caption: Note
note.Description: Represents a note or a comment in the system. Notes can be used to provide additional context, explanations, or observations related to an event, object, or any other entity in the system. They can be created and modified by users to capture important information that may not be directly represented in the structured data.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the note was created.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the note was last modified.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The user who created or last modified the note. Typically the same user that created the note can modify the note.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A short description of the comment, if applicable.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the note, if applicable.

object.Name: object
object.Caption: Object
object.Description: An unordered collection of attributes. It defines a set of attributes available in all objects. It can be also used as a generic object to log objects that are not otherwise defined by the schema.

observable.Name: observable
observable.Caption: Observable
observable.Description: The observable object is a pivot element that contains related information found in many places in the event.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier (metadata.uid) of the source OCSF event from which this observable was extracted. This field enables linking observables back to their originating event data when observables are stored in a separate location or system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The full name of the observable attribute. The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name. Array attributes may be represented in one of three ways. For example: resources.uid, resources[].uid, resources[0].uid.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Contains the original and normalized reputation scores.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The observable value type name.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The observable value type identifier.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The observable data type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which may contain data source specific value.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The OCSF event type UID (type_uid) of the source event that this observable was extracted from. This field enables filtering and categorizing observables by their originating event type. For example: 300101 for Network Activity (class_uid 3001) with activity_id 1.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The value associated with the observable attribute. The meaning of the value depends on the observable type.
If the name refers to a scalar attribute, then the value is the value of the attribute.
If the name refers to an object attribute, then the value is not populated.

observation.Name: observation
observation.Caption: Observation
observation.Description: A record of an observed value or event that captures the timing and frequency of its occurrence. Used to track when values/events were first detected, last detected, and their total occurrence count.

count.caption: Count
count.description: Integer representing the total number of times this specific value/event was observed across all occurrences. Helps establish prevalence and patterns.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time window when the value or event was first observed. It is used to analyze activity patterns, detect trends, or correlate events within a specific timeframe.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The specific value, event, indicator or data point that was observed and recorded. This is the core piece of information being tracked.

occurrence_details.Name: occurrence_details
occurrence_details.Caption: Occurrence Details
occurrence_details.Description: Details about where in the target entity, specified information was discovered. Only the attributes, relevant to the target entity type should be populated.

cell_name.caption: Cell Name
cell_name.description: The cell name/reference in a spreadsheet. e.g A2

column_name.caption: Column Name
column_name.description: The column name in a spreadsheet, where the information was discovered.

column_number.caption: Column Number
column_number.description: The column number in a spreadsheet or a plain text document, where the information was discovered.

end_line.caption: End Line
end_line.description: The line number of the last line of the file, where the information was discovered.

json_path.caption: JSON Path
json_path.description: The JSON path of the attribute in a json record, where the information was discovered

page_number.caption: Page Number
page_number.description: The page number in a document, where the information was discovered.

record_index_in_array.caption: Record Index in Array
record_index_in_array.description: The index of the record in the array of records, where the information was discovered. e.g. the index of a record in an array of JSON records in a file.

row_number.caption: Row Number
row_number.description: The row number in a spreadsheet, where the information was discovered.

start_line.caption: Start Line
start_line.description: The line number of the first line of the file, where the information was discovered.

organization.Name: organization
organization.Caption: Organization
organization.Description: The Organization object describes characteristics of an organization or company and its division if any. Additionally, it also describes cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) logical hierarchies such as AWS Organizations, Google Cloud Organizations, Oracle Cloud Tenancies, and similar constructs.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, Widget, Inc. or the AWS Organization name .

ou_name.caption: Org Unit Name
ou_name.description: The name of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, the GCP Project Name , or Dev_Prod_OU .

ou_uid.caption: Org Unit ID
ou_uid.description: The unique identifier of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, an Oracle Cloud Tenancy ID , AWS OU ID , or GCP Folder ID .

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, an AWS Org ID or Oracle Cloud Domain ID .

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

os.Name: os
os.Caption: Operating System (OS)
os.Description: The Operating System (OS) object describes characteristics of an OS, such as Linux or Windows.

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The operating system country code, as defined by the ISO 3166-1 standard (Alpha-2 code).

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

edition.caption: OS Edition
edition.description: The operating system edition. For example: Professional.

kernel_release.caption: Kernel Release
kernel_release.description: The kernel release of the operating system. On Unix-based systems, this is determined from the uname -r command output, for example "5.15.0-122-generic".

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The operating system name.

sp_name.caption: OS Service Pack
sp_name.description: The name of the latest Service Pack.

sp_ver.caption: OS Service Pack Version
sp_ver.description: The version number of the latest Service Pack.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the operating system.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type identifier of the operating system.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OS running on the device that originated the event. For example: "Windows 10", "OS X 10.7", or "iOS 9".

osint.Name: osint
osint.Caption: OSINT
osint.Description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

answers.caption: Related DNS Answers
answers.description: Any pertinent DNS answers information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: MITRE ATT&CK Tactics, Techniques, and/or Procedures (TTPs) pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: Any pertinent autonomous system information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

campaign.caption: Campaign
campaign.description: The campaign object describes details about the campaign that was the source of the activity.

category.caption: Category
category.description: Categorizes the threat indicator based on its functional or operational role.

comment.caption: Analyst Comments
comment.description: Analyst commentary or source commentary about an indicator or OSINT analysis.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence of an indicator or analysis, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source or analyst.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized identifier of the confidence level, reflecting the accuracy or pertinence of the OSINT indicator or analysis. A low confidence indicates that the collected information lacked sufficient detail or accuracy to fully qualify the indicator as malicious. When the value is 99 (Other), the confidence attribute must contain the source-specific label.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the indicator was initially created or identified.

creator.caption: Creator
creator.description: The identifier of the user, system, or organization that contributed the indicator.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A detailed explanation of the indicator, including its context, purpose, and relevance.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: The specific detection pattern or signature associated with the indicator.

detection_pattern_type.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern_type.description: The detection pattern type, normalized to the caption of the detection_pattern_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

detection_pattern_type_id.caption: Detection Pattern Type ID
detection_pattern_type_id.description: Specifies the type of detection pattern used to identify the associated threat indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The detection pattern type is not mapped. See the detection_pattern_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

email.caption: Related Email
email.description: Any email information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

email_auth.caption: Related Email Authentication
email_auth.description: Any email authentication information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration date of the indicator, after which it is no longer considered reliable.

external_uid.caption: External ID
external_uid.description: A unique identifier assigned by an external system for cross-referencing.

file.caption: Related File
file.description: Any pertinent file information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

intrusion_sets.caption: Intrusion Sets
intrusion_sets.description: A grouping of adversarial behaviors and resources believed to be associated with specific threat actors or campaigns. Intrusion sets often encompass multiple campaigns and are used to organize related activities under a common label.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: Lockheed Martin Kill Chain Phases pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: Tags or keywords associated with the indicator to enhance searchability.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: Any pertinent geolocation information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp of the last modification or update to the indicator.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name.

references.caption: References
references.description: Provides a reference to an external source of information related to the CTI being represented. This may include a URL, a document, or some other type of reference that provides additional context or information about the CTI.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Any analytics related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Related reputational analysis from third-party engines and analysts for a given indicator or OSINT analysis.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: A numerical representation of the threat indicator’s risk level.

script.caption: Related Script Data
script.description: Any pertinent script information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: Represents the severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

signatures.caption: Related Digital Signatures
signatures.description: Any digital signatures or hashes related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL of an indicator or OSINT analysis, e.g., a URL back to a TIP, report, or otherwise.

subdomains.caption: Related Subdomains
subdomains.description: Any pertinent subdomain information - such as those generated by a Domain Generation Algorithm - related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

subnet.caption: Related Subnet
subnet.description: A CIDR or network block related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

threat_actor.caption: Threat Actor
threat_actor.description: A threat actor is an individual or group that conducts malicious cyber activities, often with financial, political, or ideological motives.

tlp.caption: Traffic Light Protocol
tlp.description: The Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) was created to facilitate greater sharing of potentially sensitive information and more effective collaboration. TLP provides a simple and intuitive schema for indicating with whom potentially sensitive information can be shared.

AMBER.caption: TLP:AMBER
AMBER.description: TLP:AMBER is for limited disclosure, recipients can only spread this on a need-to-know basis within their organization and its clients. Note that TLP:AMBER+STRICT restricts sharing to the organization only. Sources may use TLP:AMBER when information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risk to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved. Recipients may share TLP:AMBER information with members of their own organization and its clients, but only on a need-to-know basis to protect their organization and its clients and prevent further harm. Note: if the source wants to restrict sharing to the organization only, they must specify TLP:AMBER+STRICT.

AMBER STRICT.caption: TLP:AMBER+STRICT
AMBER STRICT.description: TLP:AMBER is for limited disclosure, recipients can only spread this on a need-to-know basis within their organization and its clients. Note that TLP:AMBER+STRICT restricts sharing to the organization only. Sources may use TLP:AMBER when information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risk to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved. Recipients may share TLP:AMBER information with members of their own organization and its clients, but only on a need-to-know basis to protect their organization and its clients and prevent further harm. Note: if the source wants to restrict sharing to the organization only, they must specify TLP:AMBER+STRICT.

CLEAR.caption: TLP:CLEAR
CLEAR.description: TLP:CLEAR denotes that recipients can spread this to the world, there is no limit on disclosure. Sources may use TLP:CLEAR when information carries minimal or no foreseeable risk of misuse, in accordance with applicable rules and procedures for public release. Subject to standard copyright rules, TLP:CLEAR information may be shared without restriction.

GREEN.caption: TLP:GREEN
GREEN.description: TLP:GREEN is for limited disclosure, recipients can spread this within their community. Sources may use TLP:GREEN when information is useful to increase awareness within their wider community. Recipients may share TLP:GREEN information with peers and partner organizations within their community, but not via publicly accessible channels. TLP:GREEN information may not be shared outside of the community. Note: when “community” is not defined, assume the cybersecurity/defense community.

RED.caption: TLP:RED
RED.description: TLP:RED is for the eyes and ears of individual recipients only, no further disclosure. Sources may use TLP:RED when information cannot be effectively acted upon without significant risk for the privacy, reputation, or operations of the organizations involved. Recipients may therefore not share TLP:RED information with anyone else. In the context of a meeting, for example, TLP:RED information is limited to those present at the meeting.

WHITE.caption: TLP:WHITE
WHITE.description: TLP:WHITE and TLP:CLEAR may be used interchangeably, TLP:WHITE is the most up to date (as of TLP 2.0) usage.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The OSINT indicator type.

type_id.caption: Indicator Type ID
type_id.description: The OSINT indicator type ID.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The indicator type is ambiguous or there is not a related indicator for the OSINT object.

1.caption: IP Address
1.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address.

10.caption: Vulnerability
10.description: A CVE ID, CWE ID, or other identifier for a weakness, exploit, bug, or misconfiguration.

11.caption: File
11.description: A file or metadata about a file.

12.caption: Registry Key
12.description: A Windows Registry Key.

13.caption: Registry Value
13.description: A Windows Registry Value.

14.caption: Command Line
14.description: A partial or full Command Line used to invoke scripts or other remote commands.

2.caption: Domain
2.description: A full-qualified domain name (FQDN), subdomain, or partial domain.

3.caption: Hostname
3.description: A hostname or computer name.

4.caption: Hash
4.description: Any type of hash e.g., MD5, SHA1, SHA2, BLAKE, BLAKE2, SSDEEP, VHASH, etc. generated from a file, malware sample, request header, or otherwise used to identify a pertinent artifact.

5.caption: URL
5.description: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) or Uniform Resource Indicator (URI).

6.caption: User Agent
6.description: A User Agent typically seen in HTTP request headers.

7.caption: Digital Certificate
7.description: The serial number, fingerprint, or full content of an X.509 digital certificate.

8.caption: Email
8.description: The contents of an email or any related information to an email object.

9.caption: Email Address
9.description: An email address.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The indicator type is not directly listed.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the OSINT object.

uploaded_time.caption: Uploaded Time
uploaded_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the associated indicator or intelligence was added to the system or repository.

value.caption: Indicator
value.description: The actual indicator value in scope, e.g., a SHA-256 hash hexdigest or a domain name.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor name of a tool which generates intelligence or provides indicators.

vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Any vulnerabilities related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

whois.caption: WHOIS
whois.description: Any pertinent WHOIS information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

package.Name: package
package.Caption: Software Package
package.Description: The Software Package object describes details about a software package.

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of software package.

1.caption: Application
1.description: An application software package.

2.caption: Operating System
2.description: An operating system software package.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The software package version.

packet.Name: packet
packet.Caption: Packet
packet.Description: The Packet object represents a single captured network packet and its associated metadata. It describes where the packet came from, how it is stored or encoded, and how it can be located within a capture file or stream. This object does not interpret protocol content; it only represents the captured packet data and its positioning information.

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The human-readable name of the encoding used to represent the packet data in the value field. This should match the caption associated with encoding_id. If encoding_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific encoding value.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding method used to represent the packet data as a string.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The encoding format of the packet data is not known.

1.caption: Base64
1.description: The packet data is encoded using Base64.

2.caption: Hexadecimal
2.description: The packet data is encoded as a hexadecimal string representation of the raw bytes.

3.caption: URL Encoded
3.description: The packet data is encoded using percent-encoding (URL encoding).

99.caption: Other
99.description: The encoding method is not mapped. Refer to the encoding field for the original source-specific value.

end_offset.caption: End Offset
end_offset.description: The ending byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

format.caption: Format
format.description: The human-readable name of the packet capture file format in which the packet is stored. This should match the caption associated with format_id. If format_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific format value.

format_id.caption: Format ID
format_id.description: The normalized identifier of the packet capture format.

1.caption: PCAP
1.description: Standard libpcap/tcpdump packet capture file format.

2.caption: PCAPNG
2.description: Next-generation PCAP format that supports multiple interfaces and enhanced metadata.

3.caption: Snoop
3.description: Solaris/Unix capture format.

4.caption: ERF
4.description: Extensible Record Format used by Endace network monitoring hardware.

5.caption: NetMon
5.description: Microsoft Network Monitor capture file format.

6.caption: 5Views
6.description: Accellent 5Views packet capture format.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The packet format is not mapped. Refer to the format field for the original source-specific value.

sequence_number.caption: Sequence Number
sequence_number.description: The relative order number of this packet within its capture context (such as a PCAP file, network session, or reconstructed stream). This represents chronological capture order, distinct from both protocol-level sequencing (such as TCP sequence numbers).

source.caption: Source
source.description: The human-readable name describing how or where the packet was obtained. This should match the caption associated with source_id. If source_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific value.

source_id.caption: Source ID
source_id.description: A normalized numeric identifier that specifies how the packet was obtained or generated.

1.caption: Wire
1.description: The packet was captured directly from a network interface.

2.caption: Stream
2.description: The packet was reconstructed or derived from a stream of packets.

3.caption: Decoder
3.description: The packet was generated or extracted by a protocol decoder or analysis engine.

4.caption: TAP
4.description: The packet was captured from a physical network Test Access Point (TAP) device used for passive monitoring.

5.caption: SPAN
5.description: The packet was captured from a switch Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) or mirror port.

6.caption: Endpoint
6.description: The packet was captured by a host-based agent or endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor.

7.caption: Virtual
7.description: The packet was captured from a virtual network interface, virtual switch, or container network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The packet source is not mapped. Refer to the source field for the original source-specific value.

start_offset.caption: Start Offset
start_offset.description: The starting byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The actual packet data, represented as a string. The format of this string is determined by the specified encoding_id (e.g., Base64, Hexadecimal, or URL Encoded).

parameter.Name: parameter
parameter.Caption: Parameter
parameter.Description: The Parameter object provides details regarding a parameter of a a function.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The parameter name.

post_value.caption: Post-Value
post_value.description: The parameter value after function execution.

pre_value.caption: Pre-Value
pre_value.description: The parameter value before function execution.

peripheral_device.Name: peripheral_device
peripheral_device.Caption: Peripheral Device
peripheral_device.Description: The peripheral device object describes the properties of external, connectable, and detachable hardware.

class.caption: Class
class.description: The class of the peripheral device.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the peripheral device.

type.caption: Peripheral Device Type
type.description: The Peripheral Device type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Peripheral Device Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized peripheral device type ID.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The peripheral device type is unknown.

1.caption: External Storage
1.description: The peripheral device is an external storage device.

2.caption: Keyboard
2.description: The peripheral device is a keyboard.

3.caption: Mouse
3.description: The peripheral device is a mouse.

4.caption: Printer
4.description: The peripheral device is a printer.

5.caption: Monitor
5.description: The peripheral device is a monitor.

6.caption: Microphone
6.description: The peripheral device is a microphone.

7.caption: Webcam
7.description: The peripheral device is a webcam.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The peripheral device type is not mapped. See the type attribute which contains an event source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the peripheral device.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vendor_id_list.caption: Vendor ID List
vendor_id_list.description: The list of vendor IDs for the peripheral device.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The primary vendor name for the peripheral device.

permission_analysis_result.Name: permission_analysis_result
permission_analysis_result.Caption: Permission Analysis Result
permission_analysis_result.Description: The Permission Analysis object describes analysis results of permissions, policies directly associated with an identity (user, role, or service account). This evaluates what permissions an identity has been granted through attached policies, which privileges are actively used versus unused, and identifies potential over-privileged access. Use this for identity-centric security assessments such as privilege audits, dormant permission discovery, and least-privilege compliance analysis.

analyzed_privileges_count.caption: Analyzed Privileges Count
analyzed_privileges_count.description: The total count of privileges that were analyzed across all services.

condition_keys.caption: Condition Keys
condition_keys.description: The condition keys and their values that were evaluated during policy analysis, including contextual constraints that affect permission grants. These conditions define when and how permissions are applied. Examples: aws:SourceIp:1.2.3.4, aws:RequestedRegion:us-east-1.

granted_privileges.caption: Granted Privileges
granted_privileges.description: The specific privileges, actions, or permissions that are explicitly granted by the analyzed policy. Examples: AWS actions like s3:GetObject, ec2:RunInstances, iam:CreateUser; Azure actions like Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read; or GCP permissions like storage.objects.get.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Detailed information about the policy document that was analyzed, including policy metadata, version, type (identity-based, resource-based, etc.), and structural details. This provides context for understanding the scope and nature of the permission analysis.

service_privilege_analysis_list.caption: Service Privilege Analysis List
service_privilege_analysis_list.description: The list of privilege analysis results grouped by cloud service or namespace.

total_potential_attacks_count.caption: Total Potential Attacks Count
total_potential_attacks_count.description: The total count of privilege-to-attack technique mappings identified across all analyzed privileges.

unused_privileges_count.caption: Unused Privileges Count
unused_privileges_count.description: The total count of privileges or actions defined in the policy that have not been utilized within the analysis timeframe. This metric helps identify over-privileged access and opportunities for privilege reduction to follow the principle of least privilege. High counts may indicate policy bloat or excessive permissions.

unused_services_count.caption: Unused Services Count
unused_services_count.description: The total count of cloud services or resource types referenced in the policy that have not been accessed or utilized within the analysis timeframe. This helps identify unused service permissions that could be removed to reduce attack surface. Examples: AWS services like S3, SQS, IAM, Lambda; Azure services like Storage, Compute, KeyVault; or GCP services like Cloud Storage, Compute Engine, BigQuery.

policy.Name: policy
policy.Caption: Policy
policy.Description:
The Policy object describes the policies that are applicable.

Policy attributes provide traceability to the operational state of the security product at the time that the event was captured, facilitating forensics, troubleshooting, and policy tuning/adjustments.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the policy such as the underlying JSON policy itself or other details.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the policy.

is_applied.caption: Applied
is_applied.description: A determination if the content of a policy was applied to a target or request, or not.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The policy name. For example: AdministratorAccess Policy.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The policy type. For example: Identity Policy, Resource Policy, Service Control Policy, etc..

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier of the policy instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The policy version number.

port_info.Name: port_info
port_info.Caption: Port Information
port_info.Description: The Port Information object describes a port and its associated protocol details.

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

prev_event.Name: prev_event
prev_event.Caption: Previous Event
prev_event.Description: The Previous Event object references the previous event in a chain of events. Refer to specific usage.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the previous event, binding this reference to the previous event's content so that altering or substituting the previous event breaks the link. Refer to specific usage.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event type identifier of the previous event, as carried in that event's type_uid. It directs a consumer to the event class, and therefore the table or store, where the previous event resides.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the previous event, as carried in that event's metadata.uid.

privilege_attack_info.Name: privilege_attack_info
privilege_attack_info.Caption: Privilege Attack Info
privilege_attack_info.Description: The Privilege Attack Info object groups privileges by the potential attack they could enable. It maps specific privileges to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, helping identify security risks associated with granted permissions.

attack.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® Details
attack.description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique that these privileges could enable.

privilege_info_list.caption: Privilege Info List
privilege_info_list.description: The list of privilege information objects, where each element describes a specific privilege that could enable the associated attack technique.

privilege_info.Name: privilege_info
privilege_info.Caption: Privilege Info
privilege_info.Description: The Privilege Info object describes information about a specific privilege, action, or permission. It captures the privilege name, type, usage status, and when it was last used.

is_unused.caption: Is Unused
is_unused.description: Indicates whether the privilege is unused within the analysis timeframe.

last_used_time.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time.description: The most recent time this privilege was used.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the privilege, action, or permission. Examples: GetObject, CreateStoreImageTask (AWS); Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read (Azure); storage.objects.get (GCP).

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type or category of the privilege, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized type of the privilege.

1.caption: Read
1.description: A read-type privilege that permits viewing or retrieving data. Examples: s3:GetObject, Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read, storage.objects.get.

2.caption: Write
2.description: A write-type privilege that permits creating, modifying, or deleting data. Examples: s3:PutObject, Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write, storage.objects.create.

3.caption: Execute
3.description: An execute-type privilege that permits running operations or invoking functions. Examples: lambda:InvokeFunction, Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The privilege type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

process.Name: process
process.Caption: Process
process.Description: The Process object describes a running instance of a launched program.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that this process is running or hosting, if applicable. Populate when the process serves as the runtime environment for an AI agent (e.g., a Python process executing a LangChain agent or hosting an MCP server). When a process hosts multiple agents and the activity cannot be attributed to one specifically, use hosted_ai_agent_list instead.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

auid.caption: Audit User ID
auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

container.caption: Container
