token.Name: token
token.Caption: Token
token.Description: The Token object is the base object for representing tokens, API keys, and authentication credentials used across different contexts. This object provides common attributes for all token types, including protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) and API/client tokens used for service authentication. When to use this object: Use the base token object directly in API activity events to represent API tokens, client tokens, or API keys used to authenticate API requests. Examples include: Okta API tokens, Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Stripe API keys, AWS API keys. When NOT to use this object: Do NOT use the base token object for protocol-specific authentication tokens in authentication events - use authentication_token instead (which extends this object). Do NOT use token for tracking credential lifecycle and usage patterns - use programmatic_credential instead.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time that the token was created.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the token.

is_renewable.caption: Renewable
is_renewable.description: Indicates whether the token is renewable.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The last time the token was updated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The human-friendly name of a token or key, if available, such as the name from the Okta API Token API.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The unique identifier of the tenant or organization that owns the token or key, or the tenant context in which the token is authorized for use. This is particularly relevant in multi-tenant Identity Provider scenarios where tokens are scoped to specific tenants.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the token, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. This indicates whether the token is a Client Token, API Token, or one of the protocol-specific token types.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized token type identifier. Valid values: 0 (Unknown), 1 (Ticket Granting Ticket - Kerberos), 2 (Service Ticket - Kerberos), 3 (Identity Token - OIDC), 4 (Refresh Token - OIDC), 5 (SAML Assertion), 6 (Client Token - IdP-issued), 7 (API Token - generic API keys), 99 (Other).

1.caption: Ticket Granting Ticket
1.description: Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) for Kerberos.

2.caption: Service Ticket
2.description: Service Ticket (ST) for Kerberos.

3.caption: Identity Token
3.description: Identity (ID) Token for OIDC.

4.caption: Refresh Token
4.description: Refresh Token for OIDC.

5.caption: SAML Assertion
5.description: Authentication Assertion for SAML.

6.caption: Client Token
6.description: Client Token issued by an Identity Provider (IdP) for application authentication. Use this value for IdP-issued tokens used for service-to-service authentication. Examples: Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Okta API tokens, Auth0 Machine-to-Machine tokens. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by Identity Providers, not by individual services.

7.caption: API Token
7.description: A generic API token or API key used for authenticating API requests. Use this value for service-specific API authentication tokens that are NOT issued by Identity Providers. Examples: REST API keys, GraphQL API keys, Stripe API keys, Twilio API keys, AWS API keys. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by individual services/platforms, not by Identity Providers.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique ID of a token or key, if available, such as the Secret ID of Entra ID Application Registration Client Secrets.

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or geographic region that the token or key is authorized to be used from. This may represent network-based access restrictions, geographic limitations, or other zone-based authorization policies. Examples include Okta's network zone restrictions or cloud provider region restrictions.

trace.Name: trace
trace.Caption: Trace
trace.Description: The trace object contains information about a distributed trace,  which is crucial for observability. Traces are made up of one or more spans, which are individual units of work in application activity. Traces track the journey of a request as it moves through various services in a system, capturing key details like timing, status, and dependencies at each step. Traces provide insights into system performance, helping to identify latency, bottlenecks, and issues in complex, distributed environments.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The total time, in milliseconds, that the trace covers, calculated as the difference between start_time and end_time. This duration helps assess the overall performance of a request as it travels across various services, and is essential for identifying latency and potential bottlenecks within the distributed system. The trace duration may differ from individual span durations due to the propagation and processing times of the trace as it spans multiple components.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end timestamp of the trace, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the start time, this timestamp is normalized across the trace system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time allows for accurate trace duration calculations and helps observability tools track overall performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The flags associated with the trace, used to indicate specific properties or behaviors, such as whether the trace is sampled or if it has special handling. Flags help control how traces are processed, logged, and analyzed, providing valuable context for tracing and observability tools in identifying trace characteristics or specific tracking requirements.

service.caption: Service
service.description: Identifies the service or component generating the trace, helping to track and correlate the flow of requests through various parts of a distributed system. This information is essential for understanding the role and performance of specific services within the broader context of system operations and for diagnosing issues across different components.

span.caption: Span
span.description: Represents a single unit of work or operation within a distributed trace. A span typically tracks the execution of a request across a service, capturing important details such as the operation, timestamps, and status. Spans help break down the overall trace into smaller, manageable parts, enabling detailed analysis of the performance and behavior of specific operations within the system. They are crucial for understanding latency, dependencies, and bottlenecks in complex distributed systems.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start timestamp of the trace, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the end time, this timestamp is normalized across the trace system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time enables accurate trace duration calculations and helps observability tools track performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the trace used in distributed systems and microservices architecture to track and correlate requests across various components of an application.

trait.Name: trait
trait.Caption: Trait
trait.Description: Describes a characteristic or feature of an entity that was observed. For example, this object can be used to represent specific characteristics derived from events or findings that can be surfaced as distinguishing traits of the entity in question.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The high-level grouping or classification this trait belongs to.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the trait.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the trait. For example, this can be used to indicate if the trait acts as a contributing factor (increases risk/severity) or a mitigating factor (decreases risk/severity), in the context of the related finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the trait.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

transformation_info.Name: transformation_info
transformation_info.Caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info.Description: The transformation_info object represents the mapping or transformation used.

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The transformation language used to transform the data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the transformation or mapping.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product or instance used to make the transformation

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: Time of the transformation.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the mapping or transformation.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The Uniform Resource Locator String where the mapping or transformation exists.

tsig.Name: tsig
tsig.Caption: TSIG
tsig.Description: The TSIG (Transaction Signature) object represents a TSIG resource record as defined in RFC 2845. TSIG uses a shared secret key and one-way hash function to authenticate DNS messages. Per RFC 2845, at most one TSIG record is permitted per DNS message.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The HMAC algorithm used to compute the MAC. For example: hmac-sha256.

error.caption: TSIG Error
error.description: The TSIG error, normalized to the caption of the error_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

error_id.caption: TSIG Error ID
error_id.description: The normalized TSIG-specific error code as defined in RFC 2845 and RFC 6895. This is independent of the DNS message header RCODE.

16.caption: BADSIG
16.description: TSIG signature failure.

17.caption: BADKEY
17.description: Key not recognized.

18.caption: BADTIME
18.description: Signature out of time window.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The TSIG error code is not listed. See the error attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

key_name.caption: Key Name
key_name.description: The name of the shared secret key used to sign the DNS message. For example: my-tsig-key.example.com.

unmanned_aerial_system.Name: unmanned_aerial_system
unmanned_aerial_system.Caption: Unmanned Aerial System
unmanned_aerial_system.Description: The Unmanned Aerial System object describes the characteristics, Position Location Information (PLI), and other metadata of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and other unmanned and drone systems used in Remote ID. Remote ID is defined in the Standard Specification for Remote ID and Tracking (ASTM Designation: F3411-22a).

location.caption: UAS Position Location Information
location.description: The detailed geographical location usually associated with an IP address.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the aircraft or unmanned system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the unmanned system as reported by tracking or sensing hardware.

serial_number.caption: Serial Number
serial_number.description: The serial number of the unmanned system. This is expressed in CTA-2063-A format.

speed.caption: Speed
speed.description: Ground speed of flight. This value is provided in meters per second with a minimum resolution of 0.25 m/s. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: 255 m/s.

speed_accuracy.caption: Speed Accuracy
speed_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal ground speed. Measured in meters/second.

track_direction.caption: Track Direction
track_direction.description: Direction of flight expressed as a “True North-based” ground track angle. This value is provided in clockwise degrees with a minimum resolution of 1 degree. If aircraft is not moving horizontally, use the “Unknown” value

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the UAS. For example, Helicopter, Gyroplane, Rocket, etc.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The UAS type identifier.

0.caption: Unknown/Undeclared
0.description: The UAS type is empty or not declared.

10.caption: Airship
10.description: E.g., a blimp.

11.caption: Free Fall/Parachute
11.description: Parachutes, or objects without any power or propulsion mechanism.

2.caption: Helicopter
2.description: Can also be a Multi-rotor Unmanned Aircraft (e.g., Quad-copter).

4.caption: Hybrid Lift
4.description: Fixed wing aircraft that can take off vertically.

uid.caption: UAS ID
uid.description: The primary identification identifier for an unmanned system. This can be a Serial Number (in CTA-2063-A format, the Registration ID (provided by the CAA, a UTM, or a unique Session ID.

uid_alt.caption: UAS Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: A secondary identification identifier for an unmanned system. This can be a Serial Number (in CTA-2063-A format, the Registration ID (provided by the CAA, a UTM, or a unique Session ID.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

uuid.caption: UTM UUID
uuid.description: The Unmanned Aircraft System Traffic Management (UTM) provided universal unique ID (UUID) traceable to a non-obfuscated ID where this UTM UUID acts as a 'session id' to protect exposure of operationally sensitive information.

vertical_speed.caption: Vertical Speed
vertical_speed.description: Vertical speed upward relative to the WGS-84 datum, measured in meters per second. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: 63 m/s.

unmanned_system_operating_area.Name: unmanned_system_operating_area
unmanned_system_operating_area.Caption: Unmanned System Operating Area
unmanned_system_operating_area.Description: The Unmanned System Operating Area object describes details about a precise area of operations for a UAS flight or mission.

aerial_height.caption: Aerial Height
aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

altitude_ceiling.caption: Altitude Ceiling
altitude_ceiling.description: Maximum altitude (WGS-84 HAE) for a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant. Measured in meters. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

altitude_floor.caption: Altitude Floor
altitude_floor.description: Minimum altitude (WGS-84 HAE) for a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant. Measured in meters. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

coordinates.caption: Coordinates
coordinates.description: A two-element array, containing a longitude/latitude pair. The format conforms with GeoJSON. For example: [-73.983, 40.719].

count.caption: Count
count.description: Indicates the number of UAS in the operating area.

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the geographical location.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The date and time at which a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant operation ends. (This field is only applicable to Network Remote ID.)

geodetic_altitude.caption: Geodetic Altitude
geodetic_altitude.description: The aircraft distance above or below the ellipsoid as measured along a line that passes through the aircraft and is normal to the surface of the WGS-84 ellipsoid. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

geodetic_vertical_accuracy.caption: Geodetic Vertical Accuracy
geodetic_vertical_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on geodetic altitude. This is based on ADS-B Geodetic Vertical Accuracy (GVA). Measured in meters.

geohash.caption: Geohash
geohash.description:
Geohash of the geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude).

Geohashing is a geocoding system used to encode geographic coordinates in decimal degrees, to a single string.

horizontal_accuracy.caption: Horizontal Accuracy
horizontal_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal position. This is based on ADS-B NACp. Measured in meters.

is_on_premises.caption: On-Premises
is_on_premises.description: Indicates whether the location is on-premises.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

@deprecated.message: Use the network_endpoint.isp or whois.isp attribute according to your use-case.

lat.caption: Latitude
lat.description: The geographical Latitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: 42.361145.

locations.caption: Operating Polygon
locations.description: A list of Position Location Information (PLI) (latitude/longitude pairs) defining the area where a group or Intent-Based Network Participant operation is taking place. (This field is only applicable to Network Remote ID.)

long.caption: Longitude
long.description: The geographical Longitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: -71.057083.

postal_code.caption: Postal Code
postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

pressure_altitude.caption: Pressure Altitude
pressure_altitude.description: The uncorrected barometric pressure altitude (based on reference standard 29.92 inHg, 1013.25 mb) provides a reference for algorithms that utilize 'altitude deltas' between aircraft. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m.. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the geographical location data.

radius.caption: Operating Area Radius
radius.description: Farthest horizontal distance from the reported location at which any UA in a group may be located (meters). Also allows defining the area where an Intent-Based Network Participant operation is taking place. Default: 0 m.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The alphanumeric code that identifies the principal subdivision (e.g. province or state) of the country. For example, 'CH-VD' for the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The date and time at which a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant operation starts. (This field is only applicable to Network Remote ID.)

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of operating area. For example, Takeoff Location, Fixed Location, Dynamic Location.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The operating area type identifier.

0.caption: Unknown/Undeclared
0.description: The UA type is empty or not declared.

url.Name: url
url.Caption: Uniform Resource Locator
url.Description: The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) object describes the characteristics of a URL.

categories.caption: Website Categorization
categories.description: The Website categorization names, as defined by category_ids enum values.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Domain/URL category is not mapped. See the categories attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain portion of the URL. For example: example.com in https://sub.example.com.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The URL host as extracted from the URL. For example: www.example.com from www.example.com/download/trouble.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The URL path as extracted from the URL. For example: /download/trouble from www.example.com/download/trouble.

query_string.caption: HTTP Query String
query_string.description: The query portion of the URL. For example: the query portion of the URL http://www.example.com/search?q=bad&sort=date is q=bad&sort=date.

resource_type.caption: Resource Type
resource_type.description: The context in which a resource was retrieved in a web request.

scheme.caption: Scheme
scheme.description: The scheme portion of the URL. For example: http, https, ftp, or sftp.

subdomain.caption: Subdomain
subdomain.description: The subdomain portion of the URL. For example: sub in https://sub.example.com or sub2.sub1 in https://sub2.sub1.example.com.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL string. See RFC 1738. For example: http://www.example.com/download/trouble.exe. Note: The URL path should not populate the URL string.

user.Name: user
user.Caption: User
user.Description: The User object describes the characteristics of a user/person or a security principal.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The user's account or the account associated with the user.

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the user, as reported by the product.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the user is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

full_name.caption: Full Name
full_name.description: The full name of the user, as reported by the product.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The administrative groups to which the user belongs.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Assigned
has_mfa.description: The user has a multi-factor or secondary-factor device assigned.

ldap_person.caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The username. For example, janedoe1.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the user.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Details about the programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated to the user.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the user. For example, System, AWS IAM User, etc.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The account type identifier.

1.caption: User
1.description: Regular user account.

2.caption: Admin
2.description: Admin/root user account.

3.caption: System
3.description: System account. For example, Windows computer accounts with a trailing dollar sign ($).

4.caption: Service
4.description: Service account. For example, Windows service account.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique user identifier. For example, the Windows user SID, ActiveDirectory DN or AWS user ARN.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory user GUID or AWS user Principal ID.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vendor_attributes.Name: vendor_attributes
vendor_attributes.Caption: Vendor Attributes
vendor_attributes.Description:
The Vendor Attributes object can be used to represent values of attributes populated by the Vendor/Finding Provider. It can help distinguish between the vendor-provided values and consumer-updated values, of key attributes like severity_id.
The original finding producer should not populate this object. It should be populated by consuming systems that support data mutability.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The finding severity, as reported by the Vendor (Finding Provider). The value should be normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The finding severity ID, as reported by the Vendor (Finding Provider).

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

vulnerability.Name: vulnerability
vulnerability.Caption: Vulnerability Details
vulnerability.Description: The vulnerability is an unintended characteristic of a computing component or system configuration that multiplies the risk of an adverse event or a loss occurring either due to accidental exposure, deliberate attack, or conflict with new system components.

advisory.caption: Security Advisory
advisory.description: Detail about the security advisory, that is used to publicly disclose cybersecurity vulnerabilities by a vendor.

affected_code.caption: Affected Code
affected_code.description: List of Affected Code objects that describe details about code blocks identified as vulnerable.

affected_packages.caption: Affected Software Packages
affected_packages.description: List of software packages identified as affected by a vulnerability/vulnerabilities.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The category of a vulnerability or weakness, as reported by the source tool, such as Container Security or Open Source Security.

cve.caption: CVE
cve.description: Describes the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) details related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) details related to the vulnerability.

dependency_chain.caption: Dependency Chain
dependency_chain.description: Information about the chain of dependencies related to the issue as reported by an Application Security or Vulnerability Management tool. E.g., serverless-offline -> @serverless/utils -> memoizee -> es5-ext.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the vulnerability.

exploit_last_seen_time.caption: Exploit Last Seen Time
exploit_last_seen_time.description: The time when the exploit was most recently observed.

exploit_ref_url.caption: Exploit URL
exploit_ref_url.description: The URL of the exploit code or Proof-of-Concept (PoC).

exploit_requirement.caption: Exploit Requirement
exploit_requirement.description: The requirement description related to any constraints around exploit execution.

exploit_type.caption: Exploit Type
exploit_type.description: The categorization or type of Exploit. E.g., Network or Physical.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The time when the vulnerability was first observed.

fix_available.caption: Fix Availability
fix_available.description: Indicates if a fix is available for the reported vulnerability.

fix_coverage.caption: Fix Coverage
fix_coverage.description: The fix coverage, normalized to the caption of the fix_coverage_id value.

fix_coverage_id.caption: Fix Coverage ID
fix_coverage_id.description: The normalized identifier for fix coverage, applicable to this vulnerability. Typically useful, when there are multiple affected packages but only a subset have available fixes.

1.caption: Complete
1.description: All affected packages and components have available fixes or patches to remediate the vulnerability.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: Only some of the affected packages and components have available fixes or patches, while others remain vulnerable.

3.caption: None
3.description: No fixes or patches are currently available for any of the affected packages and components.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The fix coverage is not mapped. See the fix_coverage attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_exploit_available.caption: Exploit Availability
is_exploit_available.description: Indicates if an exploit or a PoC (proof-of-concept) is available for the reported vulnerability.

is_fix_available.caption: Fix Availability
is_fix_available.description: Indicates if a fix is available for the reported vulnerability.

kb_article_list.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_article_list.description: A list of KB articles or patches related to an endpoint. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

kb_articles.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_articles.description: The KB article/s related to the entity. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The time when the vulnerability was most recently observed.

packages.caption: Software Packages
packages.description: List of vulnerable packages as identified by the security product

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the vulnerability.

related_vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerability IDs
related_vulnerabilities.description: List of vulnerability IDs (e.g. CVE ID) that are related to this vulnerability.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: The remediation recommendations on how to mitigate the identified vulnerability.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The vendor assigned severity of the vulnerability.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the discovered vulnerability.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor that identified the vulnerability.

web_resource.Name: web_resource
web_resource.Caption: Web Resource
web_resource.Description: The Web Resource object describes characteristics of a web resource that was affected by the activity/event.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the resource was created.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Details of the web resource, e.g, file details, search results or application-defined resource.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: Description of the web resource.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the web resource.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The web resource type as defined by the event source.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the web resource.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL pointing towards the source of the web resource.

whois.Name: whois
whois.Caption: WHOIS
whois.Description: The resources of a WHOIS record for a given domain. This can include domain names, IP address blocks, autonomous system information, and/or contact and registration information for a domain.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The autonomous system information associated with a domain.

created_time.caption: Registered At
created_time.description: When the domain was registered or WHOIS entry was created.

dnssec_status_id.caption: DNSSEC Status ID
dnssec_status_id.description: Describes the normalized status of DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) for a domain.

1.caption: Signed
1.description: The related domain enables the signing of DNS records using DNSSEC.

2.caption: Unsigned
2.description: The related domain does not enable the signing of DNS records using DNSSEC.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The DNSSEC status is not mapped. See the dnssec_status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain name corresponding to the WHOIS record.

email_addr.caption: Registrar Abuse Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address for the registrar's abuse contact

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Updated At
last_seen_time.description: When the WHOIS record was last updated or seen at.

name_servers.caption: Name Servers
name_servers.description: A collection of name servers related to a domain registration or other record.

phone_number.caption: Registrar Abuse Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone number for the registrar's abuse contact

status.caption: Domain Status
status.description: The status of a domain and its ability to be transferred, e.g., clientTransferProhibited.

subdomains.caption: Subdomains
subdomains.description: An array of subdomain strings. Can be used to collect several subdomains such as those from Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs).

subnet.caption: Subnet Block
subnet.description: The IP address block (CIDR) associated with a domain.

win_resource.Name: win_resource
win_resource.Caption: Windows Resource
win_resource.Description: The Windows resource object describes a resource object managed by Windows, such as mutant or timer.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the resource was created.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

details.caption: Details
details.description: The string detailing the attributes of the resource object.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the resource object.

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The Windows service acting as the object server for the resource object, such as Security or Security Account Manager.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the Windows resource object.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized type identifier of the Windows resource object accessed.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The resource object type is unknown.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The resource object type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which may contain a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The Windows provided handle identifier for the resource object

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

win_service.Name: win_service
win_service.Caption: Windows Service
win_service.Description: The Windows Service object describes a Windows service.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch the service.

hosting_process.caption: Hosting Process
hosting_process.description: The process that is hosting this service.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated with the service.

load_order_group.caption: Load Order Group
load_order_group.description: The name of the load ordering group of which this service is a member.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The unique name of the service.

service_category.caption: Service Category
service_category.description: The service category, normalized to the caption of the service_category_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_category_id.caption: Service Category ID
service_category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service category.

1.caption: Kernel Mode
1.description: A kernel mode driver.

2.caption: User Mode
2.description: A user mode service.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service category is not mapped. See the service_category attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

service_dependencies.caption: Service Dependencies
service_dependencies.description: The names of other services upon which this service has a dependency.

service_dll_file.caption: Service DLL
service_dll_file.description: For a shared user mode service (service_type_id is 4) this is the DLL that gets loaded by the generic service host process (e.g. svchost.exe) to implement the service.

service_error_control.caption: Service Error Control
service_error_control.description: The service error control, normalized to the caption of the service_error_control_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_error_control_id.caption: Service Error Control ID
service_error_control_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service error control.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The service error control is unknown.

1.caption: Ignore
1.description: The startup program ignores the error and continues the startup operation.

2.caption: Normal
2.description: The startup program logs the error in the event log but continues the startup operation.

3.caption: Severe
3.description: The startup program logs the error in the event log. If the last-known-good configuration is being started, the startup operation continues. Otherwise, the system is restarted with the last-known-good configuration.

4.caption: Critical
4.description: The startup program logs the error in the event log, if possible. If the last-known-good configuration is being started, the startup operation fails. Otherwise, the system is restarted with the last-known good configuration.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service error control is not mapped. See the service_error_control attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

service_file.caption: Service File
service_file.description:
For a user mode service (service_type_id 3 or 4) this is the executable program that the SCM launches as the service process.
For a kernel mode driver (service_type_id 1 or 2) this is the driver file loaded into the kernel at the request of the SCM.

service_start_name.caption: Service Start Name
service_start_name.description: For a user mode service, this attribute represents the name of the account under which the service is run. For a kernel mode driver, this attribute represents the object name used to load the driver.

service_start_type.caption: Service Start Type
service_start_type.description: The service start type, normalized to the caption of the service_start_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_start_type_id.caption: Service Start Type ID
service_start_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service start type.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The service start type is unknown.

1.caption: Boot
1.description: A kernel mode driver loaded at boot.

2.caption: System
2.description: A kernel mode driver loaded during system startup.

3.caption: Auto
3.description: A user mode service started automatically during system startup.

4.caption: Demand
4.description: A user mode service started on demand when a process calls StartService.

5.caption: Disabled
5.description: A driver or service that cannot be started.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service start type is not mapped. See the service_start_type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

service_type.caption: Service Type
service_type.description: The service type, normalized to the caption of the service_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_type_id.caption: Service Type ID
service_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service type.

1.caption: Kernel Driver
1.description: A kernel mode driver.

2.caption: File System Driver
2.description: A kernel mode file system minifilter.

3.caption: Own Process
3.description: A user mode service that runs in its own process.

4.caption: Share Process
4.description: A user mode service that shares a process with other services.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service type is not mapped. See the service_type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the service.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the service.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the service.

account_change.Name: account_change
account_change.Caption: Account Change
account_change.Description: Account Change events report when specific user account management tasks are performed, such as a user/role being created or role assigned, changed, deleted, renamed, disabled, enabled, locked out or unlocked.

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

2.caption: Denied
2.description: The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

3.caption: Observed
3.description: The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.

4.caption: Modified
4.description: The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

1.caption: Create
1.description: A user/role was created.

10.caption: MFA Factor Enable
10.description: One or more authentication factors were enabled for a user account.

11.caption: MFA Factor Disable
11.description: One or more authentication factors were disabled for a user account.

12.caption: Unlock
12.description: A user account was unlocked.

2.caption: Enable
2.description: A user/role was enabled.

3.caption: Password Change
3.description: An attempt was made to change a user account's password.

4.caption: Password Reset
4.description: An attempt was made to reset a user account's password.

5.caption: Disable
5.description: A user/role was disabled.

6.caption: Delete
6.description: A user/role was deleted.

7.caption: Attach Policy
7.description: An IAM Policy was attached to a user/role.

8.caption: Detach Policy
8.description: An IAM Policy was detached from a user/role.

9.caption: Lock
9.description: A user account was locked out.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: Details about the authentication factors associated with the MFA Factor Enable/Disable activities.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

delegation.caption: Delegation
delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.

10.caption: Exonerated
10.description: A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).

11.caption: Corrected
11.description: A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.

12.caption: Partially Corrected
12.description: A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.

13.caption: Uncorrected
13.description: A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.

14.caption: Delayed
14.description: An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.

15.caption: Detected
15.description: Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.

16.caption: No Action
16.description: The outcome of an operation had no action taken.

17.caption: Logged
17.description: The operation or action was logged without further action.

18.caption: Tagged
18.description: A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.

19.caption: Alert
19.description: The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.

2.caption: Blocked
2.description: Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

20.caption: Count
20.description: Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.

21.caption: Reset
21.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.

22.caption: Captcha
22.description: Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.

23.caption: Challenge
23.description: Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.

24.caption: Access Revoked
24.description: The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.

25.caption: Rejected
25.description: A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

26.caption: Unauthorized
26.description: An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.

27.caption: Error
27.description: An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

3.caption: Quarantined
3.description: A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.

4.caption: Isolated
4.description: A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.

5.caption: Deleted
5.description: A file or other content was deleted.

6.caption: Dropped
6.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.

7.caption: Custom Action
7.description: A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

8.caption: Approved
8.description: A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.

9.caption: Restored
9.description: A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.caption: Enrichments
enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Details about the underlying HTTP request.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Details about the underlying HTTP response.

is_alert.caption: Alert
is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.caption: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.caption: Message Context
message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.caption: OSINT
osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policies.caption: Policies
policies.description: Details about the IAM policies associated with the Attach/Detach Policy activities.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the IAM policy associated to the Attach/Detach Policy activities.

raw_data.caption: Raw Data
raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.caption: Raw Data Hash
raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.caption: Raw Data Size
raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.caption: Risk Details
risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Details about the source of the IAM activity.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

1.caption: Success
1.description: The activity completed successfully.

2.caption: Failure
2.description: The activity failed.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that was a target of an activity.

user_result.caption: User Result
user_result.description: The result of the user account change. It should contain the new values of the changed attributes.

admin_group_query.Name: admin_group_query
admin_group_query.Caption: Admin Group Query
admin_group_query.Description: Admin Group Query events report information about administrative groups.

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

2.caption: Denied
2.description: The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

3.caption: Observed
3.description: The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.

4.caption: Modified
4.description: The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

1.caption: Query
1.description: The discovered results are via a query request.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.

10.caption: Exonerated
10.description: A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).

11.caption: Corrected
11.description: A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.

12.caption: Partially Corrected
12.description: A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.

13.caption: Uncorrected
13.description: A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.

14.description: An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.

15.description: Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.

16.description: The outcome of an operation had no action taken.

17.caption: Logged
17.description: The operation or action was logged without further action.

18.caption: Tagged
18.description: A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.

19.caption: Alert
19.description: The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.

2.caption: Blocked
2.description: Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

20.caption: Count
20.description: Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.

21.caption: Reset
21.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.

22.caption: Captcha
22.description: Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.

23.caption: Challenge
23.description: Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.

24.caption: Access Revoked
24.description: The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.

25.caption: Rejected
25.description: A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

26.caption: Unauthorized
26.description: An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.

27.caption: Error
27.description: An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

3.caption: Quarantined
3.description: A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.

4.caption: Isolated
4.description: A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.

5.caption: Deleted
5.description: A file or other content was deleted.

6.caption: Dropped
6.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.

7.caption: Custom Action
7.description: A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

8.caption: Approved
8.description: A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.

9.caption: Restored
9.description: A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

query_info.caption: Query Info

query_result_id.caption: Query Result ID
query_result_id.description: The normalized identifier of the query result.
