Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

1.caption: Create
1.description: One or more web resources were created.

2.caption: Read
2.description: One or more web resources were read / viewed.

3.caption: Update
3.description: One or more web resources were updated.

4.caption: Delete
4.description: One or more web resources were deleted.

5.caption: Search
5.description: A search was performed on one or more web resources.

6.caption: Import
6.description: One or more web resources were imported into an Application.

7.caption: Export
7.description: One or more web resources were exported from an Application.

8.caption: Share
8.description: One or more web resources were shared.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

delegation.caption: Delegation
delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.

10.caption: Exonerated
10.description: A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).

11.caption: Corrected
11.description: A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.

12.caption: Partially Corrected
12.description: A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.

13.caption: Uncorrected
13.description: A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.

14.caption: Delayed
14.description: An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.

15.caption: Detected
15.description: Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.

16.caption: No Action
16.description: The outcome of an operation had no action taken.

17.caption: Logged
17.description: The operation or action was logged without further action.

18.caption: Tagged
18.description: A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.

19.caption: Alert
19.description: The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.

2.caption: Blocked
2.description: Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

20.caption: Count
20.description: Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.

21.caption: Reset
21.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.

22.caption: Captcha
22.description: Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.

23.caption: Challenge
23.description: Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.

24.caption: Access Revoked
24.description: The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.

25.caption: Rejected
25.description: A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

26.caption: Unauthorized
26.description: An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.

27.caption: Error
27.description: An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

3.caption: Quarantined
3.description: A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.

4.caption: Isolated
4.description: A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.

5.caption: Deleted
5.description: A file or other content was deleted.

6.caption: Dropped
6.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.

7.caption: Custom Action
7.description: A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

8.caption: Approved
8.description: A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.

9.caption: Restored
9.description: A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: Details about server providing the web resources.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.caption: Enrichments
enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Details about the underlying HTTP request.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Details about the HTTP response, if available.

is_alert.caption: Alert
is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.caption: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.caption: Message Context
message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

osint.caption: OSINT
osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

proxy_connection_info.caption: Proxy Connection Info
proxy_connection_info.description: The connection information from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The proxy (server) in a network connection.

proxy_http_request.caption: Proxy HTTP Request
proxy_http_request.description: The HTTP Request from the proxy server to the remote server.

proxy_http_response.caption: Proxy HTTP Response
proxy_http_response.description: The HTTP Response from the remote server to the proxy server.

proxy_tls.caption: Proxy TLS
proxy_tls.description: The TLS protocol negotiated between the proxy server and the remote server.

proxy_traffic.caption: Proxy Traffic
proxy_traffic.description: The network traffic refers to the amount of data moving across a network, from proxy to remote server at a given point of time.

raw_data.caption: Raw Data
raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.caption: Raw Data Hash
raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.caption: Raw Data Size
raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.caption: Risk Details
risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Details about the endpoint from which the request originated.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

1.caption: Success
1.description: The activity completed successfully.

2.caption: Failure
2.description: The activity failed.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

tls.caption: TLS
tls.description: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) attributes, if available.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

updated_web_resources.caption: Updated Web Resources
updated_web_resources.description: The intended state of the web_resources after the update. On Success, represents the actual post-update state.

web_resources.caption: Web Resources
web_resources.description: Describes details about web resources that were affected by an activity/event.

web_resources_result.caption: Web Resources Result
web_resources_result.description: The results of the activity on web resources. It should contain the new values of the changed attributes of the web resources.

windows_resource_activity.Name: windows_resource_activity
windows_resource_activity.Caption: Windows Resource Activity
windows_resource_activity.Description: Windows Resource Activity events report when a process accesses a Windows managed resource object, successful or otherwise.

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

2.caption: Denied
2.description: The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

3.caption: Observed
3.description: The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.

4.caption: Modified
4.description: The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

category_uid.caption: Category ID

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

osint.caption: OSINT
osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

raw_data.caption: Raw Data
raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.caption: Raw Data Hash
raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.caption: Raw Data Size
raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

risk_details.caption: Risk Details
risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

1.caption: Success
1.description: The activity completed successfully.

2.caption: Failure
2.description: The activity failed.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

win_resource.caption: Windows Resource
win_resource.description: The Windows resource object that was accessed, such as a mutant or timer.

windows_service_activity.Name: windows_service_activity
windows_service_activity.Caption: Windows Service Activity
windows_service_activity.Description: Windows Service Activity events report when a process interacts with the Service Control Manager.

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

2.caption: Denied
2.description: The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

3.caption: Observed
3.description: The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.

4.caption: Modified
4.description: The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.
Refer to the win_service attribute for details, unless any other attribute is mentioned.

1.caption: Create
1.description: A service is created, for example by calling the CreateService API.

2.caption: Reconfigure
2.description: A service is reconfigured, for example by calling the ChangeServiceConfig or ChangeServiceConfig2 API. Refer to prev_win_service and win_service attributes for details.

3.caption: Start
3.description: A stopped service is started, for example by calling the StartService API.

4.caption: Stop
4.description: A running or paused service is stopped, for example by calling the ControlService or ControlServiceEx API.

5.caption: Pause
5.description: A running service is paused, for example by calling the ControlService or ControlServiceEx API.

6.caption: Continue
6.description: A paused service is continued, for example by calling the ControlService or ControlServiceEx API.

7.caption: Delete
7.description: A service is deleted, for example by calling the DeleteService API.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

delegation.caption: Delegation
delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.

10.caption: Exonerated
10.description: A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).

11.caption: Corrected
11.description: A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.

12.caption: Partially Corrected
12.description: A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.

13.caption: Uncorrected
13.description: A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.

14.caption: Delayed
14.description: An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.

15.caption: Detected
15.description: Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.

16.caption: No Action
16.description: The outcome of an operation had no action taken.

17.caption: Logged
17.description: The operation or action was logged without further action.

18.caption: Tagged
18.description: A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.

19.caption: Alert
19.description: The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.

2.caption: Blocked
2.description: Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

20.caption: Count
20.description: Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.

21.caption: Reset
21.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.

22.caption: Captcha
22.description: Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.

23.caption: Challenge
23.description: Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.

24.caption: Access Revoked
24.description: The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.

25.caption: Rejected
25.description: A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

26.caption: Unauthorized
26.description: An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.

27.caption: Error
27.description: An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

3.caption: Quarantined
3.description: A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.

4.caption: Isolated
4.description: A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.

5.caption: Deleted
5.description: A file or other content was deleted.

6.caption: Dropped
6.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.

7.caption: Custom Action
7.description: A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

8.caption: Approved
8.description: A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.

9.caption: Restored
9.description: A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.caption: Enrichments
enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.caption: Alert
is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.caption: Malware

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

message.caption: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

message_context.caption: Message Context
message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.caption: Observables

Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

prev_win_service.caption: Previous Windows Service
prev_win_service.description: The Windows service before the mutation.

win_service.caption: Windows Service
win_service.description: The current Windows service. On failed or unknown status of Reconfigure action may be populated with the intended state.

Dictionary.description: The Attribute Dictionary provides a comprehensive catalog of standardized attributes used across OCSF. It defines each attribute's properties, data types, and relationships. This dictionary serves as the authoritative reference for attribute definitions and ensures consistent usage throughout the schema.

access_analysis_result.caption: Access Analysis Result
access_analysis_result.description: Describes access relationships and pathways between identities, resources, focusing on who can access what and through which mechanisms. This evaluates access levels (read/write/admin), access types (direct, cross-account, public, federated), and the conditions under which access is granted. Use this for resource-centric security assessments such as external access discovery, public exposure analysis, etc.

access_level.caption: Access Level
access_level.description: The access level of an entity. See specific usage.

access_list.caption: Access List
access_list.description: The list of requested access rights.

access_mask.caption: Access Mask
access_mask.description: The access mask in a platform-native format.

access_result.caption: Access Check Result
access_result.description: The list of access check results.

access_type.caption: Access Type
access_type.description: The type or category of access being granted to the identity. See specific usage.

accessed_time.caption: Accessed Time
accessed_time.description: The time when the file was last accessed.

accessor.caption: Accessor
accessor.description: The name of the user who last accessed the object.

accessors.caption: Accessors
accessors.description: A list of users who have access to an entity. See specific usage.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The account object describes details about the account that was the source or target of the activity. See specific usage.

account_switch_type.caption: Account Switch Type
account_switch_type.description: The account switch method, normalized to the caption of the account_switch_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

account_switch_type_id.caption: Account Switch Type ID
account_switch_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the account switch method.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The account switch type is unknown.

1.caption: Substitute User
1.description: A utility like sudo, su, or equivalent was used to perform actions in the context of another user.

2.caption: Impersonate
2.description: An API like ImpersonateLoggedOnUser() or equivalent was used to perform actions in the context of another user.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The account switch type is not mapped. See the account_switch_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

ack_reason.caption: Acknowledgement Reason
ack_reason.description: An integer that provides a reason code or additional information about the acknowledgment result.

ack_result.caption: Acknowledgement Result
ack_result.description: An integer that denotes the acknowledgment result of the DCE/RPC call.

action.caption: Action
action.description: The normalized caption of 'action_id' or the source specific action.

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The normalized action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition.

2.description: The attempted activity was denied.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action was not mapped. See the action attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The actor object describes details about the user/role/process that was the source of the activity. Note that this is not the threat actor of a campaign but may be part of a campaign.

actual_permissions.caption: Actual Permissions
actual_permissions.description: The permissions that were granted in a platform-native format. See specific usage.

additional_restrictions.caption: Additional Restrictions
additional_restrictions.description: The supplementary restrictions that may apply to an entity, by the virtue of a policy. See specific usage.

advisory.caption: Security Advisory
advisory.description: Detail about the security advisory, that is used to publicly disclose cybersecurity vulnerabilities by a vendor.

aerial_height.caption: Aerial Height
aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

affected_code.caption: Affected Code
affected_code.description: List of Affected Code objects that describe details about code blocks identified as vulnerable.

affected_packages.caption: Affected Software Packages
affected_packages.description: List of software packages identified as affected by a vulnerability/vulnerabilities.

agent.caption: Agent
agent.description: An Agent (also known as a Sensor) is typically installed on an Operating System (OS) and serves as a specialized software component that can be designed to monitor, detect, collect, archive, or take action. These activities and possible actions are defined by the upstream system controlling the Agent and its intended purpose. For instance, an Agent can include Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) agents, backup/disaster recovery sensors, Application Performance Monitoring or profiling sensors, and similar software.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: An autonomous AI agent that performs tasks under delegated authority. Distinguished from the OCSF agent object, which describes security sensors such as EDR and DLP tools.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI Model object describes the characteristics of an AI/ML model. Examples include language models like GPT-4, embedding models like text-embedding-ada-002, and computer vision models like CLIP.

ai_provider.caption: AI Provider
ai_provider.description: AI service provider or organization name.

ai_role_id.caption: AI Role ID
ai_role_id.description: The originator or target role of the message.

aircraft.caption: Aircraft
aircraft.description: The Aircraft object represents any aircraft or otherwise airborne asset such as an unmanned system, airplane, balloon, spacecraft, or otherwise. The Aircraft object is intended to normalized data captured or otherwise logged from active radar, passive radar, multi-spectral systems, or the Automatic Dependant Broadcast - Surveillance (ADS-B), and/or Mode S systems.

alert.caption: Client TLS Alert
alert.description: The integer value of a TLS alert per the TLS specification.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The applicable algorithm, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id'. See specific usage.

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The normalized identifier of the algorithm. See specific usage.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The algorithm is not mapped. See the algorithm attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

all_privileges_unused.caption: All Privileges Unused
all_privileges_unused.description: Indicates whether all privileges in a set, list, collection or group are unused. See specific usage.

altitude_ceiling.caption: Altitude Ceiling
altitude_ceiling.description: Maximum altitude (WGS-84 HAE) for a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant. Measured in meters. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

altitude_floor.caption: Altitude Floor
altitude_floor.description: Minimum altitude (WGS-84 HAE) for a group or an Intent-Based Network Participant. Measured in meters. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

analysis_targets.caption: Analysis Targets
analysis_targets.description: The specific dimensions, components, or aspects of the system that are the targets of the analysis. See specific usage.

analytic.caption: Analytic
analytic.description: The analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the finding or conclusion.

analyzed_privileges_count.caption: Analyzed Privileges Count
analyzed_privileges_count.description: The total count of privileges that were analyzed. See specific usage.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

anomalies.caption: Anomalies
anomalies.description: A list of detected anomalies or deviations from expected behavior patterns. See specific usage.

anomaly_analyses.caption: Anomaly Analyses
anomaly_analyses.description: A list of anomaly analysis results that examine and characterize patterns of activity or usage over time to identify normal vs abnormal activities. See specific usage.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

app.caption: Application
app.description: The application that reported the event.

app_name.caption: Application Name
app_name.description: The name of the application associated with the event or object.

app_protocol_name.caption: Application Protocol Name
app_protocol_name.description: The application protocol name. See specific usage.

app_uid.caption: Application ID
app_uid.description: The unique ID of the application associated with the event or object.

application.caption: Application
application.description: An Application describes the details for an inventoried application as reported by an Application Security tool or other Developer-centric tooling. Applications can be defined as Kubernetes resources, Containerized resources, or application hosting-specific cloud sources such as AWS Elastic BeanStalk, AWS Lightsail, or Azure Logic Apps.

applications.caption: Applications
applications.description: A list of application objects. See specific usage.

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

args.caption: HTTP Arguments
args.description: The arguments sent along with the HTTP request.

assessment.caption: Assessment
assessment.description: The Assessment object describes a point-in-time assessment, check, or evaluation of a specific configuration or signal against an asset, entity, person, or otherwise. For example, this can encapsulate os_signals from CrowdStrike Falcon Zero Trust Assessments, or account for Datastore configurations from Cyera.

assessments.caption: Assessments
assessments.description: A list of assessment objects. See specific usage.

assignee.caption: Assignee
assignee.description: The details of the user assigned to an Incident.

assignee_group.caption: Assignee Group
assignee_group.description: The details of the group assigned to an Incident.

attack.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® Details
attack.description: The MITRE ATT&CK® object describing the tactic, technique, and sub-technique.

attack_graph.caption: Attack Graph
attack_graph.description: An Attack Graph describes possible routes an attacker could take through an environment. It describes relationships between resources and their findings, such as malware detections, vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and other security actions.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

attributes.caption: Attributes
attributes.description: The bitmask value that represents the file attributes.

auid.caption: Audit User ID
auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: Describes a category of methods used for identity verification. See specific usage.

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authentication protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authentication protocol used to create the user session.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The authentication protocol is not mapped. See the auth_protocol attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

auth_type.caption: Authentication Type
auth_type.description: The agreed upon authentication type, normalized to the caption of 'auth_type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

auth_type_id.caption: Authentication Type ID
auth_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the agreed upon authentication type. See specific usage.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The authentication type is not mapped. See the auth_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

authentication_token.caption: Authentication Token
authentication_token.description: The authentication token, ticket, or assertion. See specific usage.

author.caption: Author
author.description: The author(s) who published the software component.

authority.caption: DNS Authority Section
authority.description: The DNS Authority section resource records. Contains NS records pointing to authoritative name servers, or a SOA record for negative responses (NXDOMAIN).

authority_uid.caption: Authority ID
authority_uid.description: The unique identifier of the authority that produced an attestation. See specific usage.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

autoscale_uid.caption: Autoscale UID
autoscale_uid.description: The unique identifier of the cloud autoscale configuration.

avg_timespan.caption: Average Timespan
avg_timespan.description: The average time span of an activity.

banner.caption: Protocol Banner
banner.description: The initial connection response that a messaging server receives after it connects to an email server.

base_address.caption: Base Address
base_address.description: The memory address where the module was loaded.

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The base score as reported by the event source. See specific usage.

baselines.caption: Baselines
baselines.description: A list of baseline measurements or normal behavior patterns used as reference points for comparison and anomaly detection. See specific usage.

bcc.caption: Bcc
bcc.description: The machine-readable email header Bcc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

bcc_mailboxes.caption: Bcc Mailboxes
bcc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Bcc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

binary_data.caption: Binary Data
binary_data.description: The item's data in binary form.

bios_ver.caption: BIOS Version
bios_ver.description: The BIOS version. For example: LENOVO G5ETA2WW (2.62).

body_length.caption: Body Length not including header
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP response/request body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

boot_time.caption: Boot Time
boot_time.description: The time when the system was booted.

boot_uid.caption: Boot UID
boot_uid.description: A unique identifier of the device that changes after every reboot. For example, the value of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id from Linux's procfs.

boundary.caption: Boundary
boundary.description:
The boundary of the connection, normalized to the caption of 'boundary_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary(same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

boundary_id.caption: Boundary ID
boundary_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the boundary of the connection.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary (same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

1.caption: Localhost
1.description: Local network traffic on the same endpoint.

10.caption: Gateway VPC
10.description: Through a gateway VPC endpoint (Nitro-based instances only)

11.caption: Internet Gateway
11.description: Through an Internet gateway (Nitro-based instances only)

2.caption: Internal
2.description: Internal network traffic between two endpoints inside network.

3.caption: External
3.description: External network traffic between two endpoints on the Internet or outside the network.

4.caption: Same VPC
4.description: Through another resource in the same VPC

5.caption: Internet/VPC Gateway
5.description: Through an Internet gateway or a gateway VPC endpoint

6.caption: Virtual Private Gateway
6.description: Through a virtual private gateway

7.caption: Intra-region VPC
7.description: Through an intra-region VPC peering connection

8.caption: Inter-region VPC
8.description: Through an inter-region VPC peering connection

9.caption: Local Gateway
9.description: Through a local gateway

99.caption: Other
99.description: The boundary is not mapped. See the boundary attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

bus_type.caption: Bus Type
bus_type.description: The attachment bus or interface standard, normalized to the caption of the bus_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

bus_type_id.caption: Bus Type ID
bus_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the attachment bus or interface standard.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The bus type is unknown or not reported.

1.caption: Onboard
1.description: The device is attached directly on the motherboard or SoC (often referred to as 'integrated' or 'onboard').

2.caption: PCIe x16
2.description: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express slot with 16 lanes, typically used for high‑bandwidth add‑in devices.

3.caption: PCIe x8
3.description: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express slot with 8 lanes; common for high‑performance NICs, storage controllers, and accelerators.

4.caption: MXM Type A
4.description: Mobile PCI Express Module (MXM) Type A form factor (compact laptop/embedded GPU module).

5.caption: MXM Type B
5.description: Mobile PCI Express Module (MXM) Type B form factor (larger laptop/embedded GPU module).

6.caption: M.2
6.description: M.2 (NGFF) internal module form factor/connector exposing PCIe (and/or SATA/USB) for SSDs and add‑in modules.

7.caption: CXL
7.description: Compute Express Link (CXL), an open cache‑coherent interconnect for processors, memory expansion, and accelerators built on the PCIe physical layer.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A bus or interface standard not covered by the defined values; the exact value is reported by the event source.

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The total number of bytes (in and out).

bytes_in.caption: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: The number of bytes sent from the destination to the source.

bytes_missed.caption: Bytes Missed
bytes_missed.description: Indicates the number of bytes missed, which is representative of packet loss.

bytes_out.caption: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: The number of bytes sent from the source to the destination.

campaign.caption: Campaign
campaign.description: The campaign object describes details about the campaign that was the source of the activity.

caption.caption: Caption
caption.description: A short description or caption of the device. For example: Scanner 1 or Database Manager.

categories.caption: Website Categorization
categories.description: The Website categorization names, as defined by category_ids enum values.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The object category, normalized to the caption of category_id. See specific usage.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the object category. See specific usage.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Domain/URL category is not mapped. See the categories attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by the category_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding category_uid enum value (e.g., "Findings" for category_uid: 2).

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

cc.caption: Cc
cc.description: The machine-readable email header Cc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

cc_mailboxes.caption: Cc Mailboxes
cc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Cc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

cell_name.caption: Cell Name
cell_name.description: The name of the cell. See specific usage.

certificate.caption: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate object containing information about the digital certificate.

certificate_chain.caption: Certificate Chain
certificate_chain.description: The Chain of Certificate Serial Numbers field provides a chain of Certificate Issuer Serial Numbers leading to the Root Certificate Issuer.

chain_uid.caption: Chain ID
chain_uid.description: Identifier of an append-only chain, such as a forensic or audit log, that groups a sequence of attested events for independent verification. Stable for the lifetime of the chain.

charter.caption: Charter
charter.description: A document defining the role, scope, and operating bounds of an entity. See specific usage.

chassis.caption: Chassis
chassis.description: The chassis type describes the system enclosure or physical form factor. For example, as described for a Windows chassis type.

checks.caption: Compliance Checks
checks.description: A list of specific, individual compliance verification checks derived from standard or non-standard benchmark rules or requirements.

chunks.caption: Chunks
chunks.description: A unit of information within an SCTP packet, consisting of a chunk header and chunk-specific content. See RFC 4960. This field can be used for the total number of chunks (in and out).

chunks_in.caption: Chunks In
chunks_in.description: A unit of information within an SCTP packet, consisting of a chunk header and chunk-specific content. See RFC 4960. This field can be used for the chunks sent from the destination to the source.

chunks_out.caption: Chunks Out
chunks_out.description: A unit of information within an SCTP packet, consisting of a chunk header and chunk-specific content. See RFC 4960. This field can be used for the chunks sent from the source to the destination.

cis_benchmark.caption: CIS Benchmark
cis_benchmark.description: The CIS Benchmark describes best practices for securely configuring IT systems, software, networks, and cloud infrastructure as defined by the Center for Internet Security.

cis_benchmark_result.caption: CIS Benchmark Result
cis_benchmark_result.description: The CIS Benchmark Result object captures results generated from benchmark evaluations as defined by the Center for Internet Security.

cis_controls.caption: CIS Controls
cis_controls.description: The CIS Critical Security Controls is a prioritized set of actions to protect your organization and data from cyber-attack vectors.

cis_csc.caption: CIS CSC
cis_csc.description: The CIS Critical Security Controls is a list of top 20 actions and practices an organization’s security team can take on such that cyber attacks or malware, are minimized and prevented.

class.caption: Class
class.description: The class name of the object. See specific usage.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by the class_uid value. The value must match the caption defined for the corresponding class_uid (e.g., "Detection Finding" for class_uid: 2004).

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The classification as defined by the vendor.

classification_ids.caption: Classification IDs
classification_ids.description: The list of normalized classification identifiers. See specific usage.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification is not mapped. See the classifications attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

classifications.caption: Classifications
classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

client_ciphers.caption: Client Cipher Suites
client_ciphers.description: The client cipher suites that were exchanged during the TLS handshake negotiation.

client_dialects.caption: Client Dialects
client_dialects.description: The list of SMB dialects that the client speaks.

clipboard.caption: Clipboard
clipboard.description: The clipboard that pertains to the event. See specific usage.

clipboard_native_type.caption: Data Type
clipboard_native_type.description: The type of the item's data, in an operating specific form. For example: CF_TEXT or public.utf8-plain-text.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description: The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure. See specific usage.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The numeric response sent to a request.

codes.caption: Response Codes
codes.description: The list of numeric responses sent to a request.

column_name.caption: Column Name
column_name.description: The name of the column. See specific usage.

column_number.caption: Column Number
column_number.description: The number of the column. See specific usage.

community_uid.caption: Community ID
community_uid.description: The Community ID of the network connection.

company_name.caption: Company Name
company_name.description: The name of the company that published the file. For example: Microsoft Corporation.

completion_tokens.caption: Completion Tokens
